parties:
Md. Sirajul Haque
Vs.
Sonali bank ltd. chandaikona branch, raiganj, sirajganj and others
full_judgment:
Quazi Reza-Ul Hoque, J: In the instant writ petition Rule NISI was issued calling upon the respondent No.1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 25.10.2007 passed by the learned District Judge, Sirajganj in Artha Rin Miscellaneous Appeal No. 01 of 2006 condoning the delay of 7 years 10 months and 7 days and admitting the appeal for hearing (annexure-A) should not be declared to have been done without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/ or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. And pending hearing of the Rule, the operation of the impugned order was stayed for a period of three (3) months, which was extended from time to time, lastly on 08.07.2010 till disposal of the Rule.

2. The petitioners case, in short, is that the respondent No.1 as plaintiff filed Money Suit No. 13/1986 against Angaha Pat Chaski (APACHAS), Raiganj Unit No. 3, Raiganj and 5(five) others including the petitioner as defendant No. 2 for recovery of money in the Court of learned Sub-Ordinate Judge, Sirajganj, stating inter alia that under Bangladesh Jute Project, IDA Credit-765-RD to provide marketing Credit to marketing Centres, during 1982-83 season, Angsha Pat ChashiSamity (ARACHAS), Raiganj Unit No. 3, the defendant No. 1, the present petitioner was as its President was sanctioned with a loan cash credit limit of TK. 4,00,000/-(four lacs) by the plaintiff bank by letter No. RCD05/-29/40 dated 10.08.1982 at a simple interest rate of 12% per annum. The loan was repayable and fully adjustable by 30.04.1983. The then Jute Extension Officer Abdul Kuddus has been succeeded by defendant No. 5 and defendant Nos. 2- 5 were jointly and severally liable for the debt and repayment of the loan as it was secured through a Demand Promissory Note amounting to Tk. 4 lacs on 29.11.82 in favour of the plaintiff bank. The defendants failed to repay the loan. The service charges and penal interests were stipulated at the rate of 4% and 6% respectively per annum.

3. The account of the defendants with effect from 01.10.83 under RCD Circular No. 85 dated 11.01.83 was confirmed by the defendants. The balance was confirmed on 05.01.83 for TK. 1,31,080.50; as on 31.12.83, 31.12.85 and 01.01.86 for TK. 71,042.50 and the defendants acknowledged the loan by signing a revival letter on 31.01.84. On 01.01.86 by a unanimous resolution dated 07.12.82 of APACHAS, Raiganj Unit No. 3 Md. Serajul Haque, Chairman resigned from his office and handed over charge, which was accepted by the defendant No. 4, the then Secretary, Md. Abdul Wahed Mondal. An amount of TK.88,809.50 as per statements of accounts dated 31.08.86 of the defendants remained outstanding against them in spite of repeated demands and in that regard legal notice dated 16.01.86 was served upon them.

4. On 21.05.1988 the suit was decreed ex parte behind the back of the petitioner, without considering the actual facts and circumstances and true evidences on record. After coming to know about the ex pane decree against him the defendant-petitioner filed Miscellaneous Case No. 30/90 by filing an application under order- 9, rule- 13 of the Civil Procedure Code, 1908 to cancel and set aside the ex parte decree and re-instate the suit to its original file and number. The learned Judge of the Artho Rin Adalat, after hearing the said petition on 23.01.1991 rejected the said petition.

5. The defendant- petitioner after coming to know from a news item in the Daily Janakantha dated 06.05.1997 that the scheduled property of the original Money Suit No. 77 of 1996, corresponding Execution Case No. 9 of 1994 will be auction-sold, filed Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1997 under order 21, rule 58 read with section 151 of the Civil Procedure Code stating inter alia that he is not at all indebted to the opposite party bank. The father of the petitioner sold a portion of the scheduled property else where long ago. The petitioner's brother, sister and wife are the owners of the rest of the scheduled property and therefore the same is not liable to be auctioned. The judgment-creditor has illegally obtained a decree for auction, and as such, the petitioner is entitled to be exonerated from the obligation of the suit.

6. The actual fact is that the plaintiff bank sanctioned a loan of TK. 4,00,000/- (four lacs) to the defendant Samity for purchasing jute during 1982-83 and at that time the petitioner was the Chairman of the Samity. The petitioner, as Chairman of the Samity drew TK. 75,000/- form the bank on 29.11.1982 and thereafter the plaintiff- petitioner with that money purchased 550 mounds of jute at the rate of TK. 150/- per mound and deposited the purchased jute in bank's go-down. The defendant- petitioners resigned from his post due to his serious illness on 07.12.1982 in the meeting No. 6 of 82 of the Committee, which the Committee accepted and released him from the post of Chairman of the Samity and in the same meeting all the responsibilities were assigned to the Secretary, Abdul Wahed Mondol. The plaintiff- bank was informed of the decision taken in the said meeting No. 6 of 82 dated 17.12.82. So the defendant petitioner had no liability in respect of the said loan. The matter of purchasing 550 mounds of jute with the said loan of Tk. 758,000/- was admitted at the said meeting of the Samity. The defendant- petitioner prayed for statements of accounts from the bank and the bank through letter dated 21.12.82 addressed to the Samity stated that he has no liability for the period during which the defendant- petitioner was its Chairman. The jute deposited by the petitioner was sold away by the manager of the bank on 31.05.83 and on 01.06.83 and the entire sale-proceeds amounted to TK. 76,420/-, which was deposited in the account of the Samity with the bank and receipt thereof had been obtained. A part of the property under 'auction notice' was decreed in favour of Oke Gedi Bibi in Suit No. 6 of 1986 on 02.12.1970, by the learned Court of Subordinate Judge, Pabna, and as such, the said property was also eligible to be released from auction notice.

7. The opposite party No. 1, i.e. bank, filed written objection stating inter alia that the petitioner as Chairman of the Angsha Pat Chashi Samity, Raiganj Unit- 3 took a loan of TK. 75,000/- from the bank and did not repay the same according to the terms of the loan for which the opposite party bank filed Money Suit No. 13 of 1986 for recovery of the loan and got a decree on 22.05.1988. Due to non-payment of the decreetal amount the Execution Case No. 14 of 1989 was filed against the petitioner and others and after establishment of Artha Rin Adalat the case was transferred and re-numbered as Artha Rin Case No. 77 of 1990 and then after transfer to the Artho Rin Adalat No. 2, it was re-numbered as Case No. 9 of 1994. The scheduled property of the petitioner was attached on 14.11.1990 and the same was approved by the Court on 26.11.1990. The case of the petitioner is barred by limitation and suffers from defect of parties; and the scheduled land is owned and possessed by the petitioner.

8. Artha Rin Adalat- 2 framed only one issue as to whether the petitioner is entitled to get the remedy as prayed for and on careful perusal of the papers and evidence on record the Court found that the loan of TK. 75,000/-drawn by the petitioner as Chairman of the Samity has already been adjusted by purchasing 500 mounds of jute at the rate of TK. 150/- per mound and keeping the same in bknk's godown, which had been admitted by the bank and subsequently by selling the said jute by the bank and depositing the sale proceeds in the account of the Samity, the loan was fully adjusted and the same had been admitted by the bank in a letter addressed to the Samity. After considering papers and evidence on record and the depositions made on behalf of the parties the learned Artha Rin Adalat came to the finding that the petitioner is entitled to get the relief as prayed for and allowed the Miscellaneous Case on contest passed on order on 23.08.1998 to release suit property from the schedule of the Execution Case No. 9 of 1994.

9. The opposite party bank filed Artho Rin Miscellaneous Appeal No. 1 of 2006 on 20.08.2006 in the Court of District Judge, Sirajganj against the said judgment and order along with an application for condonation of delay of 7 years 10 months and 7 days under section 5 of the Limitation Act read with section 57 of the Artha Rin Ain. The Court of Appeal below on 25.10.2007, that is, after filing of the appeal and the condonation petition in the court of the learned District Judge and registering the same as Miscellaneous Appeal No. 01 of 2006 on 20.08.2006 the condonation petition was disposed of 25.10.2007, condoning the delay and allowing the appeal (annexure- A and A 1 ).

10. Mr. Abul Kalam, the learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioner submitted that the Artho Rin Adalat disposed of the Miscellaneous Case No. 01 of 1997 on 23.08.1998 and according to Artho Rin Adalat Ain an appeal against the judgment and order should have been filed within 30 days. But the opposite party bank sent the relevant papers to the learned lawyer on 13.10.1998 i.e. on the 30th day of passing of the judgment and order consuming the whole period of limitation sitting idle. So there is serious laches and negligence on the part of the appellant bank. Therefore it was not possible on the part of the learned lawyer to file the appeal within the statutory limitation of 30 days after receiving the relevant papers on the 30th day after passing of the judgment and order.

11. He further submitted that the reasons for delay of 7 years 10 months and 7 days as explained by the appellant bank are not at all sufficient and tenable in the eye of law. The learned Court of Appeal below committed an error of law not considering the fact that the impugned judgment and order was passed by the Artho Rin Adalat on 23.08.1998, the application for certified copy was filed after 3 days on 26.08.1998. Certified copy of the judgment and order was ready for delivery on 17.08.1998 and thereafter the relevant papers for filing appeal were sent to the concerned lawyer on 13.10.1998, i.e. after expiry of the statutory period of limitation of 30 days and that has not been explained at all in the application for condonation of delay, which indicates grave laches and negligence on the part of the opposite party No.1, which resulted to an error in decision occasioning failure of justice.

<u>12. The learned court of appeal below committed error of law not considering that the entire amount of loan of TK. 75,000/-drawn by the petitioner as the Chairman of the Samity had been fully adjusted by the petitioner by purchasing 550 monds of jute at the rate of TK. 150/- per mond and depositing the same in the bank's godown, which was sold by the bank and the sale proceeds credited in to the loan account of the Samity kept with the bank and the loan taken by he petitioner had been fully adjusted and this error of law committed by the learned Court of Appeal below resulted to an error in decision occasioning a serious failure of justice.</u>

<u>13. On perusal of the writ petition and supplementary affidavit, we find that the explanation of delay given in the application filed under section 5 of the Limitation Act, is not sufficient and tenable in the eye of law. It appears that the learned District judge condoned the delay without issuing any notice upon the applicant-writ-petitioner. The said impugned order passed by the learned District Judge totally ignored the law considering the application field under Order 21 Rule LVIII and thereby allowed it. A close scrutiny of the Artha Rin Ain, 1990, shows that there was a clear provision for appeal within 30 days. As it was a special law, so condoning the delay is beyond the jurisdiction of the learned District Judge. The bank could avail the opportunity for filing the appeal before the District Judge, which it did not, rather resorted to filing the appeal after 7 years 10 months and 7 days, which do not appear to us as tenable in law. And therefore we find that the impugned order as being passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.</u>

14. In the result, the Rule is made absolute.

15. The impugned Order passed by the learned District Judge, Sirajganj dated 25.10.07 in Artha Rin Miscellaneous Appeal No. 01 of 2006, is hereby declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and therefore it is set aside.

16. There is no order as to costs.

17. Send a copy of this judgment and order to the concerned Court below immediately.

End.

parties:
S.M. Mohiuddin Hossain
Vs.
Jalalabad Co-Operative Housing Society Limited and others
full_judgment:
Syed Abu Kowser Md. Dabirush-Shan, J: This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No.1 to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 02.04.2003 and 08.04.2003 respectively passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Sadar, Chittagong in Other Appeal No.03 of 1996 allowing the appeal and thereby reversing the judgment and decree dated 29.08.1995 and 05.09.1995 respectively passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, 5th Court, Sadar, Chittagong in Other Suit No.121 of 1992 should not be set aside.

2. The petitioner being sole plaintiff instituted the suit for permanent injunction in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, 5th Court, Sadar, Chittagong on 19.11.1992 being Other Suit No.3 of 1995 with a prayer for permanent injunction and the restrain to defendants from entering into the suit property and not to evict plaintiff and not to do any harm to the properties and houses therein.

3. The suit of the plaintiff case is that the land described in Schedule-"Ka" of the plaint was belonged to the R. S. record of tenant and on successive transfer ultimately Zafar Ahmed became owner by purchase and possessed the same. The area of R.S. Plot No.95 is 1.37 acres and the area of land described in Schedule-"Ka" of the plaint is .37 decimals of land. Zafar Ahmed being owner in possession sold the same to the plaintiff by a registered kabala dated 30.08.1976 on proper consideration and put the plaintiff in possession over the "Ka" Schedule land and since then the plaintiff has been in exclusive possession and the name of the plaintiff has been mutated by separating the jama in Mutation Case No.2649/1991-92 and his name was also recorded in the B.S. Khatian by order dated 09.06.1992. The plaintiff for his exclusive use constructed the boundary walls in all sides of the "Ka" Schedule land and also put barbed wires on the wall running from North to West and north to south and the plaintiff also has his own path way connecting the Government Road. The plaintiff also constructed a tinshed semi pacca house having iron pillars at the western side of the suit plot and in the thatched fencing tinshed house darwans are residing. The plaintiff also sinks a tubewell for drinking water and planted coconut trees, bamboo trees and also used to cultivate seasonal crops. Since the date of purchase of the "Ka" Schedule land the defendants have been trying to grab the property and for that end and view they started conspiracy. The plaintiff resides away from the suit land and taking this advantage the darwans and other employees of the plaintiff have been threatening to dispossess by the defendant for which the plaintiff submitted application to the Deputy Commissioner, Police Commissioner and other authorities informing about the illegal activities of the defendants. The plaintiff also got his land measured through Additional Deputy Commissioner, Revenue and the defendants threatened to demolish the plaintiff's new constructed wall and house. On measurement of the area of land it was found correct that there was a path way from North to South by the eastern side of the suit plot from the time of his predecessor Jafar Ahmed for public use. The defendants have no right title and interest and also possession in any manner in the suit land. The plaintiff took loan from Agrani Bank, Agrabad Hotel Branch by mortgaging the "Ka" Schedule land. The defendants have been threatening to dispossess and also have been creating obstruction in the use of the path way and as such the plaintiff constrained to file the suit for perpetual injunction.

4. The defendant No.1 appeared and contested the suit by filing written statement and also denied the material allegation made in the plaint by the written statement and it has been stated that the plaintiff has no cause of action for filing the suit and the suit is not maintainable. The suit is barred by limitation and further stated that the defendant No.1 is a Co-Operative Housing Society which was established in 1975 and in order to solve the acute housing problem of the City Dweller of Chittagong and with that end and view he purchased the vast land for this noble purpose. The defendant also obtained permission from Chittagong Development Authority to cut hills on 04.07.1975 and got passed the layout plan for constructing the building over the land of the defendant and C.D.A. also approved the said plan on 25.10.1976 and gave permission to cut hill of the extended area. Zafar Ahmed sold 1(one) acre of land out of R.S. Plot No.95 by kabala dated 31.08.1976 to the defendant No.1 and handed over possession accordingly and B.S. Khatian has been published in his name. The plaintiff also purchased .37 decimals of land from the said Zafar Ahmed and entered into an agreement with the defendant No. 1 in order to develop the land after cutting hill and the plaintiff became member of the society and in lieu of two plots of the society he had relinquished his claim over .37 decimals of land in favour of the defendant No.1 in the first part of 1983 and accordingly handed over the possession of the said land to defendant -1 and also assured the defendant No.1 to pay Tk.10,000/- towards development cost and also assured to pay more money if necessary. The defendant developed the land along with the said .37 decimals of land allotted to one Mustafa Younus Noor, M.A. Matin, Md. Shafi Ahmed, Md. Shamsuddin, and Dilruba Jahan and accordingly executed the lease deed in favour of those persons and as per the terms of agreement the defendant kept one plot for the plaintiff. The plaintiff also wrote a letter to that effect on 07.04.1985. There are few plots in the schedule land and also a pathway over the suit land as per layout plan and the defendants also made all arrangement for taking water and electricity connection for the use in the plots. The defendants also guarding to protect the society land and properties, But one Abdul Hamid instituted a suit claiming 67½ decimals of land against the defendant as plaintiff in the Court of Assistant Judge in 1987 being Other Suit No.70 of 1987 and the plaintiff in spite of service of summons did not appear in that suit but defendant contest the suit and ultimately the suit was dismissed for default. The plaintiff on ill advised by one Mintu and also finding that the value of land has substantially been increased due to the development made by the defendant, hence the plaintiff filed the suit and as such the suit is liable to be dismissed.

5. During the course of trial the learned Assistant Judge after concluding the trial and on consideration of the evidence on record both oral and documentary decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiff by his judgment and decree dated 29.08.1995 and 05.09.1995 respectively.

6. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree passed by the trial court the defendant preferred an appeal before the learned District Judge, Chittagong and the appeal was ultimately heard and disposed of by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Sadar, Chittagong who was pleased to allow appeal and reversed the judgment and decree passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, 5th Court, Sadar, Chittagong and thereby the suit is dismissed without considering the plaint, written statement and evidence both oral and documentary and only on the basis of surmise and conjecture by his judgment and decree dated 02.04.2003 and 08.04.2003 respectively.

7. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Sadar, Chittagong, the plaintiff-respondent-petitioner preferred the instant revisional application before the High Court Division under Section-115 of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present Rule.

8. The learned Counsel Mr. Momotazuddin Ahmed with Mr. Md. Abu Taleb appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-respondent-petitioner submits that the appellate court is absolutely wrong and erroneous in reversing the judgment and decree passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, 5th Court, Sadar, Chittagong. Next he submits that the learned Senior Assistant Judge, 5th Court, Sadar, Chittagong after going through the evidence on record and after scrutinizing the evidence on record clearly and elaborately discussed the evidence and taking into consideration the facts and circumstances of the case and also the legal aspect of the case came to a proper and justified finding in decreeing the suit in favour of the plaintiff. Whereas the learned joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Sadar, Chittagong without applying his judicial mind and without proper assessment of the evidence on record and without discussing the evidence on record and by misreading of evidence came to a wrong and fallacious finding in reversing the judgment and decree passed by the trial court which is absolutely wrong and illegal and liable to be set aside. The learned Counsel further submits that the appellate court in reversing the finding of the trial court is required to reverse the finding with reference to the evidence on record but in the instant suit the appellate court without referring the evidence on record and without considering the evidence on record and by misreading of the evidence came to a wrong and preposterous finding occasioning failure of justice which is liable to be interfered by this court. The learned Counsel finally submits that the lower appellate court without applying his judicial mind and without assigning any cogent ground and reason reverse the judgment of the trial court which is absolutely on the basis of surmise and conjecture and not passed on facts and evidence on the record which is liable to be interfered by this court and hence the Rule should be made absolute. The learned Counsel in support of his contention referred the case of Md. Afazuddin-Versus- Moyezuddin Shaikh being dead his heirs Tahejuddin Shaikand and others reported in 5 B.L.D. (AD) 54 wherein it has been held that:

"Reversal of Judgment-Reversal of the trial court's judgment without adverting to the evidence on which the trial Court's judgment is based is not a proper <u>Judgment of Reversal</u> in the circumstances of the case High Court Division misdirected itself refusing to interfere with the decision of the lower appellate court."

9. On the other hand, Mr. H.S. Deb Brahman the learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the defendant-appellant-opposite parties submits that the lower appellate court is absolutely right and justified in reversing the judgment and decree passed by the trial court. Next he submits that the appellate court after going through the evidence on record and applying his judicial mind came to a correct and proper finding in dismissing the suit and also submits that the suit land is vague and unspecified and the plaintiff could not state any boundary of the suit land in his plaint and as such the learned appellate court rightly observed in his judgment that the suit land is vague and unspecified and as such no permanent injunction can be given, The learned Counsel further submits that the defendant is the Secretary of Jalalabad Co-Operative Housing Society Limited and the plaintiff is also one of the members of that society. The plaintiff cannot file a suit before the Civil Court directly without lodging any complain before the Registrar of Co-Operative and the Civil Court has got no jurisdiction to take up a suit or legal proceedings against the Secretary of Co-Operative Society. Therefore the civil suit against the defendant is a bar under Section-133 of the Co-Operative Society Ordinance, 1984. The learned Counsel finally submits that there was no cause of action for this suit and the plaintiff did not prove the cause of action in his suit and there was no prima facie case for permanent injunction and as such the lower appellate court rightly and correctly reversed the judgment and decree passed by the trial court in decreeing the suit in favour of the plaintiff and hence the Rule should be discharged.

<u>10. On a meticulous examination of the evidence on record, judgment and decree passed by the lower appellate court as well as the trial court it transpires that the lower appellate court without applying his judicial mind and without proper assessment of the evidence on record and without assigning any cogent ground and reason reversed the judgment of the trial court which is not legally tenable. The lower appellate court while reversing the judgment of the trial court is required to reverse the material findings of the trial court with reference to the material evidence on record under Order-41, Rule-31 but in the instant suit the lower appellate court without referring the evidence on record and without assigning any cogent ground and reason reversed the judgment and decree passed by the trial court which is liable to be interfered by this court. The trial court in his judgment after an elaborate discussion of the evidence on record and after considering the material facts and circumstances of the case came to a proper and justified finding in decreeing the suit. It was a suit for permanent injunction and in determining a suit for permanent injunction the factum of possession is the prime consideration before the court and the plaintiff successfully proved his title and possession by producing documentary evidence as well as oral evidence in the suit. The plaintiff examined as many as 6 (six) witnesses in this case to prove the possession who categorically stated in their evidence that the plaintiff since his purchase has been in possession of the suit land by constructing surrounding wall in the suit land. The lower appellate court by misreading and non-consideration of material evidence affecting the merit of the case and without referring the evidence on record reversed the judgment and decree passed by the trial court occasioning failure of justice which is liable to be set aside. In this connection I like to rely on the decision in the case of Ranjit Sarker and others -Versus- Sree Sukhendu Bikash Biswas and others reported in 17 B.L.D.(AD) 58 which reads as follows:</u>

<u>Order XLI Rule-31</u>

<u>Judgment of Reversal</u>

<u>"The appellate Court failed to advert to the specific reasonings of the trial Court nor did it discuss all the material evidence taken into consideration by the trial Court. The gross omission made by the appellate Court is in respect of the clear findings by the trial Court about the deed of agreement for reconveyance and the subsequent deeds of sale as genuine. This goes to the root of the merit of the case. Since no relief could be granted to the plaintiffs without coming to any finding that any of the said deeds other than the deeds of sale under pre-emption were sham transaction, the appellate Court was wrong in reversing the judgment of the trial Court in a casual manner."</u>

<u>11. In the instant suit the lower appellate court without determining the main question of dispute and without determining the title and possession of the plaintiff in a suit for permanent injunction came to a wrong finding in reversing the judgment and decree passed by the trial court, in this connection I like to referred the case of Hussain Ahmed Chowdhury alias Ahmed Hossein Chowdhury and others -Versus- Md. Nurul Amin and others reported in 47 D.L.R.(AD) 162 wherein it has been held that:</u>

<u>"If there is misreading of evidence and non-consideration of some material evidence then it was incumbent on the revisional court to consider the same and to arrive at a proper finding on the material evidence on record and to finally dispose of the case."</u>

12. In view of the facts and circumstances of the case and also the legal position, I find that the lower appellate court is absolutely wrong in reversing the judgment and decree of the trial court as such the judgment and decree passed by the lower appellate court is liable to be set aside.

13. The discussion made above and the facts and circumstances of the case and also the legal position the impugned judgment and decree dated 02.04.2003 and 08.04.2003 respectively passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Sadar, Chittagong in Other Appeal No.03 of 1996 allowing the appeal and thereby reversing the judgment and decree dated 29.08.1995 and 05.09.1995 respectively passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, 5th Court, Sadar, Chittagong in Other Suit No.121 of 1992 is hereby set aside and the judgment and decree passed by the trial court is hereby affirmed.

14. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to the cost.

15. The order of status quo issued by this court at the time of issuance of the rule is hereby vacated.

16. The lower courts record be sent down at once with a copy of the judgment.

End.

full_judgment:
Md. Abu Tariq, J: This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the judgment and order dated 15.11.2006 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court Munshigonj, in Title Execution Case No. 4 of 2006 so far as it relates to attaching 50% salary of the petitioners excepting 1st 100/- (one hundred) Taka of the basic under order 21 rule 32 (1) of the Code of Civil Procedure for a period of 1(One) year should not be set aside and after hearing the parties, perusing records and cause shown if any, make the Rule absolute and or pass such other or further order or orders may seem fit and proper.

2. Short facts for disposal of the Rule is that the opposite party No. 1 as plaintiff on 19.10.1996 instituted Title Suit No. 64 of 1996 against the petitioners and other opposite parties in the court of learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Munshigonj, praying for a decree of declaration of Title in the suit land measuring 61 decimals. The suit land is not a vested and non resident property and the R.S. record with regard to the suit land is wrong. The suit was contested by the defendant No. 3 (Present petitioner No.2). The said suit was ultimately decreed on contest against defendant No. 3 and ex-parte against rest others without cost vide judgment and decree dated 25.6.1997 and the said decree was drawn up and signed on 1.7.1997.

3. Thereafter opposite party No.1 on 17.8.2005 instituted Title Suit No. 73 of 2005 in the Court of learned Joint District Judge, Court, Munshigonj against the petitioners and other opposite parties praying for a decree for Mandatory Injunction direction upon the defendants to release the suit land from the list of vested and non resident property and to accept rent from the plaintiff on mutating the name of the plaintiff and introducing new holding with regard to the suit land.

4. The defendant No.1 of the said suit (present petitioner NO.2) contested the suit by filling written statement denying the material statements and allegations of the plaint.

5. The learned Joint District Judge Court, Munshigonj upon hearing both the parties and considering the materials on record by the judgment and decree dated 31.7.2006 decreed the suit on contest. Thereafter, the said decree was drawn up and signed on 6.8.2006 and thereby directed the defendants to mutate and introduce a new holding of the suit land on releasing the, same from the list of vested and non 655 resident property within 30 days from date.

6. Thereafter, for execution of the decree, the decree hold opposite 'party filed Title' Execution' Case No. 4 of 2006 on 15.10.2006 under Order 21 Rule 32 of the Code of Civil Procedure for violating the courts' direction and for contempt of court and for attachment of immovable and movable property of the petitioners. During pendency of the' Title Execution Case decree holder opposite party No. 1 filed an application under order 21 rule 32 (1) of the, Code of Civil Procedure 'for attachment of the monthly salary and other allowances of the petitioners till disposal of the Execution Case. The learned District Judge,1 Court , Munshigonj vide order No. 3 dated 15.11.2006 attached 50% of the salary of the.petitioners for a period of 1(one) year from date which is still pending for disposal in the 1st Court of icarned Joint District Judge, Munshigonj.

7. Hence this revision challenging the impugned order by the judgment debtor petitioners .

<u>8. Mr. Goutam Kumar Roy, the learned advocate, appearing for the petitioner submits that after expiry of the period provided in law the opposite party No. 1 as decree holder filed Title Execution Case No. 4 of 2006 on 15.10.2006 under order 21 rule 32 of the Code of Civil Procedure for violating and disobeying the court's directions and thereby for contempt of court in order to awarding of Civil Imprisonment and for attachment of salary of the petitioners which is not tenable in the eye of law. The Execution Case under order 21 rule 32 of the Code of Civil Procedure is not at all maintainable inasmuch as it is the settled principle that when a prohibitory injunction is violated the remedy is not by putting the decree into execution but by adopting other measures as provided by the law and as such the impugned order passed in the Execution Case is illegal and erroneous resulting in an error of decision occasioning failure of justice.</u>

<u>9. In a case of violation of any prohibitory order court is to see before passing any punitive order like the impugned order as to whether the judgment debtors have willfully disobeyed the prohibitory order and in the instant case the learned Joint District Judge committed an error of Law resulting in an error in the impugned decision occasioning failure of justice in not giving any finding that the judgment debtors willfully disobeyed the prohibitory order.</u>

10. Mr. Mr. Ashoke Kumar Ghose, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite parties and submits that the impugned order has been passed in accordance with law and them is nothing to interfere with and the Rule may be discharged with cost.

11. We have perused the revisional application. Heard the learned Advocate.

Order XXI Rule 32 run as follows:

(1) Where the party against whom a decree for the specific performance of a contract, or for restitution of conjugal rights, or for an injunction, has been passed, has had an opportunity of obeying the decree and has willfully failed to obey it, the decree may be enforced [in the case of a decree for restitution of conjugal rights by the attachment of his property or in the case of a decree for the specific performance of a contract or for an injunction] by his detention in the civil prison, or by the attachment of his property or by both.

(2) Where the party against whom a decree for specific performance or for an injunction has been passed is a corporation, the decree may be enforced by the attachment of the property of the corporation or, with the leave of the Court, by the detention in the civil prison of the directors or other principal officers thereof, or by both attachment and detention.

(3) ………………………………..

(4) ………………………………..

(5)………………………………..

12. It is evident and certain that a decree directing the defendants as personal designata to release the property from "ka" list of the Abandoned Property List and mutate and introduce a new holding number of the suit land cannot be executed under this Rule provided in the Code of Civil Procedure. From the aforesaid provision of the Code of Civil Procedure remedy for enibreing the decree has been provided in case of willful failure to carry out the injunction by the judgment-debtor though he had an opportunity for obeying the decree. In such case decree may be enforced the procedure laid down therein. The prohibitory injunction order does not pass with the land as by the decree no right, title and interest is created or determined in the property in the suit. In such case, it has to be decided whether for enforcing his right the petitioner will entitle to invoke the civil court's jurisdiction. The answer is negative.

13. It appears that prohibitory injunction order does not pass with the land as by the decree no decree no right, title and interest is created or determined in the property in the suit. In such case, it has to be decided whether for enforcing his right the petitioner will entitle to invoke the civil court's jurisdiction. The answer is negative.

14. It appears that decree has been found to be for release of the property and for mutation and for new holding has never been disobeyed. There is no specific allegation of willful disobedience of which makes the judgment-debtor liable for attachment of his salary. It will be pertinent to consider whether the opposite party had the opportunity to obey the decree and had willfully disobeyed or failed to obey the same. The attachment passed in the impugned order against the petitioner by names, who were the officers-in-charge from time to time is not based on any factual or legal footing.

<u>15. As such since the petitioner seek remedy in the suit and seek to enforce the same for declaration and possession it cannot be entertained by civil court. In this view of the matter also the petitioner cannot get any relief of this civil revision. There can be no doubt that if Court acts beyond jurisdiction, its action would be nullity but it does not necessarily follow from this even what it does with jurisdiction will also be rendered void because the court has at the same time done something which was without jurisdiction. It is admitted that the disputed property was enlisted in the `ka' list of Abandoned Buildings which was in possession of the government. So by operation of sub-section 2 of section 5 of Ordinance No. LIV Of 1985 the publication of disputed property in the official Gazette as abandoned property is conclusive evidence of the facts that the said property is abandoned property and has vested in the Government.</u>

<u>16. In the present case, admittedly the petitioners were out of possession on the date on which P.O. 16 /72 came into force. As such, their remedy if any, lies before the court of Settlement under Ordinance LIV of 1985. As such the petitioner had availed with the wrong forum in filing the suit and ultimately proceeding with the present impugned proceeding. The court of settlement was a court for determining whether the case property was an abandoned property or not. The civil court, i.e. Sub-Judge being not a court to determine the matter in issue and to issue mandatory injunction to implement the judgment having separate forum. The matter in issue is under the jurisdiction of settlement court under Ordinance No. 54 of 1985. The impugned order of attachment by the learned sub judge is not legally necessary to be protected as no suit lies to the civil court relating to the abandoned property and for such cause of action party is to apply to the settlement court having jurisdiction to try such cause of action.</u>

17. Considering the arguments of the parties' and all the aspects, facts and circumstances we are of the view that the opposite parties failed to show that there were willful disobedience of the decree and order of the court by these petitioners, who are now not in a position to execute the decree and the decree was not in their personal names and failed to prove any violation or disobedience of the impugned order thus attachment of salary is not sustainable in law. Moreso, when a decree is not executed, here in this case direction is not obeyed or violated, the remedy is not by putting the decree into execution but by adopting other measures as provided by law. As in this case mutation has not been done holding no has not been given etc has allegedly not been obeyed, the decree is not executable and the execution case is not maintainable for any of the remedies under Order 21 Rule 32 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

18. In the present case there is no disobedience or violation of the order of the court or decree as the remedy of the decree holder is not by putting the decree into execution but by adopting other measures as provided by law for release of the abandoned properties. Moreso, the attachment order was for 1(one) year only which is as apparent no longer existing.

19. However, the petitioners are at liberty to avail the appropriate forum to redress their grievances, if so advised.

20. Accordingly we find substance in the Rule.

21. In the result, the Rule is made absolute and impugned judgment and order is set aside. The executing court is directed to proceed with the execution case and dispose it expeditiously.

22. The order of stay granted at the time of issue of the Rule dated 16.04.2007 is hereby recalled and vacated.

End.

Fatema Begum ------- Appellants
Vs.
The Artha Rin Adalat Narayangonj and Others ------- Respondent
full_judgment:
Ruhul Quddus, J. This Rule Nisi was issued to examine the validity of order No. 76 dated 10.3.2010 (annexe-C to the writ petition) passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, Narayangonj summarily rejecting Miscellaneous Case No. 3 of 2010 filed under Order XXI Rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure and Section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 in Mortgage Decree Execution Case No. 25 of 2001 (arising out of Mortgage Suit No. 72 of 1996).

2. The petitioner's case in short is that her father late Dudu Mian was the lawful owner in possession of 8.04 decimals of land out of 20 decimals appertaining to C.S. Khatian No. 278, Dag No. 354 corresponding to S.A. Khatian No. 333, Dag No. 490 and R.S. Khatian No. 218, 226 and 371 Dag No. 459 under Mouza Dewbhoge of Police Station and District Narayanganj (more particularly described in schedule-1 of the writ petition). The petitioner, her brother and sisters inherited the said property after the demise of their father Dudu Mian and have been enjoying and possessing the same for more than twelve years without any interruption. She (petitioner) came to know from a reliable source on 18.2.2010 that their land would be auctioned in execution of a mortgage decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, Narayangonj in Mortgage Suit No. 72 of 1996. She rushed to the Court on 23.2.2010 and obtained an information slip, from which she specifically learnt that Respondent No. 2 (IFIC Bank Ltd., BB Branch, Narayanganj) had obtained a mortgage decree against Respondent No. 3, Alhaj Abul Hossain in Mortgage Suit No. 72 of 1996 from the Artha Rin Adalat, Narayangonj in respect of unspecified 7 (seven) decimals of land from the same plot. The decree holder bank put the decree in execution by filling Mortgage Decree Execution Case No. 25 of 2001, which is still pending.

3. Under the above circumstances, the petitioner, her brother and sisters filed an application for release of their property from the schedule of the mortgage suit as well as the Mortgage Decree Execution Case and also prayed for staying all further proceedings in the Mortgage Decree Execution Case till disposal of the application, which was numbered as Miscellaneous Case No. 3 of 2010. The learned Judge heard the Miscellaneous Case on maintainability and rejected the same by the impugned order dated 10.3.2010 on the ground that the petitioners did not deposit 25% of the decretal amount according to Section 32(2) of the Artha Rin Ain, 2003 (in short "the Ain, 2003").

4. The petitioner's further case is that the land in question is situated vertically from north to south. They have been possessing the same from the south-east side and the judgment debtor was possessing from the extreme north side. But as the petitioner's land is developed one in comparison to the land of the auction purchaser, he has already broken the fence around the land in order to take possession over the land in question. Since the land was never partitioned and demarcated, she instituted Title Suit No. 145 of 2008 in the First Court of Joint District Judge, Narayanganj against the decree holder bank and others for partition of the said land and filed an application for injunction therein. The learned Joint District Judge on hearing the said application passed an order on 22.7.2009 directing to maintain status quo (vide annexe-D to the writ petition). She, however, has no objection if Respondent No. 2 (bank) realizes its loan by selling the land of Respondent No. 3. She is not a "third party" within the meaning of Section 32(2) of the Ain, 2003.

5. Respondent No. 2 i.e., the decree holder bank and Respondent No. 4, the auction purchaser contested the Rule by filling two separate affidavits-in-opposition. Respondent No. 2 in its affidavit-in-opposition did not specifically deny the material facts of the writ petition except the statement that "the petitioner is not a third party of the Mortgage Decree Suit (Mortgage Decree Execution Case) No. 25 of 2001..." as stated in paragraph 8 of the writ petition. However, Respondent No. 2 denied the material facts of the writ petition in an evasive manner.

6. Respondent No. 4 filed his affidavit-in-opposition stating, inter alia, that the auction notices were published in two dailies namely "The Daily Amar Desh" and "The Daily Shitalakkha" on 2.2.2010 and 4.2.2010 respectively. In response thereto he participated in the auction bid quoting Taka 26,80,000/- and became the highest bidder. He deposited Taka 6,70,000/- on 28.2.2010 (wrongly typed as 28.10.2010 in the affidavit-in-opposition) and paid rest of the consideration (Taka 20,10,000/-) on 8.3.2010 and thereafter the Artho Rin Adalat executed and registered the "Boinama" on 6.4.2010 and delivered part possession of the auctioned land to him on 2.6.2010. The petitioner was fully aware of the mortgage suit and she has no interest in the land of Respondent No. 3 (judgment debtor). In the said affidavit-in-opposition Respondent No. 4 (auction purchaser) also disputed the right and title of the writ petitioner as well as her co-sharers over the land in question.

7. Mr. Abdur Razzaq, the learned Counsel appearing with Mr. Shahjada Al-Amin Kabir, the learned Advocate in support of the Rule submitted that the land in question is the only homestead belongs to the petitioner. She is neither a borrower nor a guarantor or a party in the suit. She does not claim the auctioned property, that has been sold to the auction purchaser. But the auction purchaser in collusion with the police force, was trying to dispossess the petitioner from her land, for which the cause of action for moving the application under Section 57 of the Ain, 2003 has arisen. The learned Counsel further submitted that since the land is not clearly and specifically mentioned in the schedule of the decree showing boundaries and location of the 7 (seven) decimals of land, that has been sold to the auction purchaser, its possession cannot be delivered in the execution proceedings without partition and demarcation of the land in question. In such circumstances, the petitioner is not required to deposit 25% of the decretal amount and Section 32(2) of the Ain, 2003 would not apply in this case. Section 57 of the said Ain gives inherent power to the Artha Rin Adalat to pass necessary order to meet the ends of justice and therefore, the impugned order rejecting the petitioner's application without deposition of 25% of the decretal amount was illegal and without lawful authority.

8. He also submitted that the plaint in the mortgage suit with no specification of the mortgaged land was not in conformity with Section 8(2)(Kha) of the Ain, 2003 and the decree foreclosing an unspecified land is itself an abuse of the process of the Court. Moreover, according to Section 33(7)(Kha) of the Ain [as amended by Artha Rin Adalat (Amendment) Ain, 2010] the executing Court is under legal obligation to make sure that a specified land was attached before giving delivery of possession to a decree holder.

9. In support of his submission, Mr. Abdur Razzaq cited one unreported judgment passed in Writ Petition No. 5180 of 2010 (Victor Rodrix and others Vs. The 4th Artha Rin Court, Dhaka and others), wherein a Division Bench of the High Court Division presided over by Justice Nazmun Ara Sultana under similar facts and circumstances held:

In a case like the present one the petitioners are not required to file an application under Section 32 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain and as such they are not required to deposit security money under the said section. Since the application filed by the petitioners under Order 21 Rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure read with Section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 was very much maintainable, the Adalat below ought to have accepted the same for consideration on merit. Thus we are inclined to dispose of this writ petition without issuance of the Rule directing upon the Artha Rin Adalat below to accept the application dated 8.3.2010 filed by the petitioners and to consider the same on merit without requiring the petitioners to deposit any security money.

10. On the other hand, Mr. M.A. Samad, the learned Counsel appearing with Mr. M.G.H. Ruhullah, the learned Advocate for Respondent No. 4 submitted that the application under Order XXI Rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure (in short "the Code") before the executing Court was not maintainable inasmuch as the sale certificate in respect of the auctioned land had already been executed and registered and the matter reached in finality. Section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 will also not apply because of having specific remedy under the law. However, the writ petitioner had remedy under Order XXI Rule 90 of the Code, which she did not avail. In support of his submission, the learned Counsel cited one unreported decision of the Appellate Division passed in Civil Appeal No. 151 of 2008 and also cited the case of Md. Delwar Hossain Vs. Bangladesh and others reported in 24 BLD (HC) 323. In course of his submission, Mr. Samad very honestly admitted that the writ petitioner and her co-sharers are in possession of 8.04 decimals of land of the same plot, but he denied their title over the same.

11. We have perused the writ petition and affidavits-in-opposition with the annexes, considered the submissions of the learned Counsels for both the parties and have gone through the decisions cited by them. It appears from the judgment of the Appellate Division passed in Civil Appeal No. 151 of 2008 that the case was between the judgment debtor and decree-holder, wherein after issuance of certificate under Section 33(5) of the Ain, 2003 and registration of the same and also mutation of the record in favour of the decree holder, the judgment-debtor filed an application under Section 57 of the Ain, 2003 read with Section 151 of the Code in the decree execution case to pay the entire decretal amount by selling the mortgaged property. It also appears that there was no controversy over the location of the land. In that case the Appellate Division held that after attainment of the decree in finality the judgment debtor has no right to redeem the mortgaged property and, that the power under Section 57 is only available when the other provisions of the Ain are not exhaustive.

12. In the present case the writ petitioner is not claiming the auctioned land. She was not a party to the suit and was neither a borrower nor a guarantor to the decree holder bank. The executing Court is still in seisin of the matter and the petitioner filed her application on 28.2.2010 i.e. before issuance of the sale certificate and also before payment of the full consideration (bid money).

<u>13. In 24 BLD (HC) 323, vires of Section 32(2) of the Ain, 2003 with an order passed by Artha Rin Adalat rejecting an application under Order XXI Rule 58 of the Code were challenged, wherein the parties were fighting over the same land and the application was filed after the mortgaged property was sold out. In the said case, the petitioner did not invoke Section 57 of the Ain, 2003. But in the present case the land of the respective parties are under claim of separate ownership, but without partition or demarcation. The application has been filed before issuance of the sale certificate and Section 57 of the Ain, 2003 is invoked. Therefore, the facts and circumstances of the cases as cited by the learned Counsel for Respondent No. 4 are distinguishable.</u>

<u>14. A plain reading of the petitioner's application under Order XXI Rule 58 of the Code read with Section 57 of the Ain, 2003 (annex-B to the writ petition) suggests that it arises out of a cause of action, which is very peculiar and uncommon. The petitioner may be a third party, but since she does not claim the auctioned property and the decree as well as the auction notice do not show that the mortgaged property is specified or clearly identified or demarcated and can easily be separated out of total land in the dag in question, Section 32(2) of the Ain, 2003 is therefore not attracted and Section 57 of the said Ain will come into play to pass necessary order to meet the ends of justice. The Respondent Nos. 2 and 4 have failed to show that 7 (seven) decimals of land, that has been auctioned, is clearly identified or demarcated. On the other hand, the petitioner has proved that a suit for partition of the scheduled land is pending between the writ petitioner and the decree holder bank and others before a competent civil Court, wherein the learned Judge has passed an order of status quo in her favour (vide annex-D to the writ petition). In such circumstances, the decree passed in a suit for foreclosure in respect of an unspecified land, cannot be fully satisfied without partition or demarcation of the decretal land. The dispute between the parties over the title and possession of the land, can be determined in proper forum, but her (petitioner's) right to property guaranteed under the Constitution can not be taken away without giving her any opportunity to prove her claim.</u>

<u>15. In deciding the point of controversy, the object of law is also to be looked into. The preamble, Sections 2(Ga), 6(5) and other provisions of the Ain, 2003 strongly suggest that the law is enacted for recovery of loan from the defaulter loanee, i.e., the borrower, guarantor, mortgagor and the persons placed in similar position. In the present case the petitioner is in no way connected with the loan, she does not claim the auctioned land and there is no cause of realisation against her. Such a person is not intended by the law to bear extra financial burden of 25% of the decretal amount as a pre-requisite to get relief.</u>

16. In view of the above we find substance in the Rule. Accordingly, the Rule is made absolute. The impugned order dated 10.3.2010 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, Narayangonj summarily rejecting Miscellaneous Case No. 3 of 2010 in Mortgage Decree Execution Case No. 25 of 2001 (arising out of Mortgage Suit No. 72 of 1996) is hereby declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

17. The learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat, Narayangonj is directed to consider/dispose of the petitioner's application being Miscellaneous Case No. 3 of 2010 in Mortgage Decree Execution Case No. 25 of 2001 on merit without deposition of 25% of the decretal amount.

18. The learned Advocate for Respondent No. 4 is permitted to take back annexes-1, 2, 3 and 4 from his affidavit-in-opposition substituting photo copies there for.

19. The office is directed to send a copy of this judgment to the Artha Rin Adalat, Narayangonj at once.

End.

Vs.
Md. Nuruzzaman
full_judgment:
Md. Muzammel Hossain, C. J. <u>This petition for leave to appeal under Article 103 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh is directed against the judgment and order dated 28.06.2009 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.3099 of 2008 making the Rule absolute.</u>

<u>2. The petitioner tiled Miscellaneous Case No.154 of 1982 in the Court of the learned District Judge, Mymensingh against the respondent under Article 27 of President's Order No.7 of 1973 for realization of Tk.6,03,407.02 which includes the principal amount as well as the interest till 31.10.1982. The Miscellaneous Case was allowed exparte on 03.04.1983. The petitioner thereafter filed Execution Case No.1 of 1986 in the Court of the learned District Judge, Mymensingh which was subsequently transferred to the Artha Rin Adalat by an administrative order of the learned District Judge and renumbered as Execution Case No.80 of 1991. The petitioner being the bidder of auction purchase of the suit land obtained the sale certificate and while making attempt to take possession of the said building with police help the respondent filed a Transfer Case being Miscellaneous Case No.74 of 1997 before the Court of the learned District Judge, Mymensingh alleging that all orders passed in the execution case was without jurisdiction and the learned District Judge by order dated 08.04.1999 held that in view of the decisions reported in 47 DLR 158 and 16 OLD (AD) 231 Artha Rin Adalat is not permitted to prosecute the execution case. In the said execution case the decree-holder filed an application for amendment of the execution petition and the executing court by impugned dated 07.05.2008 allowed the amendment of execution petition which reads as follows:</u>

<u>“উক্ত কর্পোরেশন বিগত ৩/৪/৮৩ ইং তারিখে একতরফা সূত্রে এই ডিক্রি প্রাপ্ত হইয়াছে। মূল মোকদ্দমায় দায়িক পক্ষ প্রতিদ্বন্ধিতা করেন নাই। একতরফা ডিক্রিতে আদায়কাল কত সুদ ডিক্রিদার পক্ষ প্রাপ্ত হইবেন উল্লেখ থাকায় শুধুমাত্র সুদের হিসাব করিয়া ডিক্রিদার সেই অংকটি ডিক্রীজারীর দরখাস্তে সন্নিবেশন করার আবেদন করিয়াছেন।ইহাতে আপত্তি করার কোন সুযোগ নাই। এমতাবস্থায়, দায়িক পক্ষের সময়ের আবেদন নাকচ করা হইল। পক্ষান্তরে, ডিক্রীদারপক্ষে সংশোধনী আবেদন মঞ্জুর করা হইল। ডিক্রীর জারীর দরখাস্ত ও রেজিষ্ট্রি প্রার্থিত মতে সংশোধন করা হউক।”</u>

3. The respondent being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and order dated 07,05.2008 preferred the Civil Revision No.3099 of 2008 before the High Court Division and a Division Bench of the High Court Division by the judgment and order dated 28.06.2009 made the Rule absolute.

4. Being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division, the petitioner preferred the instant civil petition for leave to appeal before this Court.

5. Mr. Shaheed Alam, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the petitioner filed the application for amendment under Order 21, Rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure so that actual amount due to be shown in the decree because this would not affect the claim of the petitioner and the same was reasonable and fair, but the High Court Division wrongly appreciated the fact and set aside the order passed by the learned District Judge. He then submits that the petitioner was a party in auction sale and as such respondent has no locus-standi to raise objection as to the amount which will not affect the interest of the respondent. He finally submits that the respondent without filing any application to set aside the auction cannot raise any objection to an order passed under order 21 rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure, but the High Court Division wrongly passed the impugned order which has affected the interest of House Building Finance Corporation and as such leave should be granted.

6. Mr. Md. Mozibar Rahman, the learned Advocate-on-Record for the respondent submits that there is no illegality in the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division and as such no interference is called for. The learned Advocate-on-Record for the respondent having referred to Order 21, Rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure submits that Rule 17(1) of Order 21 of the Code refers only to the requirements of Rules 11-14 as may be applicable to the case and in the instant case the alleged defect in execution application has no reference to Rules 11-14 of Order 21, inasmuch as the exparte order dated 04.03.1983 passed by the learned District Judge in Miscellaneous Case No.154 of 1982 does not contain any direction upon the defendant respondent to pay interest from the date of the exparte order till realization and as such this Rule does not apply to allow the petitioner to rectify the mistake in the application for execution and that the learned Judges of the High Court Division having considered this aspect of the matter rejected the prayer for amendment of the application for execution in making the Rule absolute by the impugned judgment and order, as such there is no illegality in the impugned judgment and order. Mr. Md. Mozibar Rahman having referred to the order dated 03.04.1983 passed by the learned District Judge submits that since there is no specific order for interest till realizations of the decreetal amount, the learned District Judge as an executing Court has clearly travelled beyond the order which is to be executed by imposing interest till realization of the amount and as such the High Court Division committed no illegality in making the Rule absolute by setting aside the order passed by the learned District Judge.

<u>7. We have heard the learned Advocates appearing for both the parties, perused the leave petition, impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division and all other connected papers on record. In the instant case the petitioner filed Miscellaneous Case No. 154 of 1982 in the Court of learned District Judge, Mymensingh against the judgment-debtor-respondent under Article 27 of President's Order No.7 of 1973 for realization of Tk.6,03,407.02 which includes the principal with interest till 31.10.1982. The decree holder-petitioner obtained exparte order on 03.04.1983. Thereafter on the basis of the said exparte decree Execution Case No.1 of 1986 was filed in the Court of the learned District Judge, Mymensingh which was subsequently transferred to the Court of Artha Rin Adalat by an administrative order of the learned District Judge and renumbered as Execution Case No.80 of 1991. The respondent having come to know about the Execution Case filed a Transfer Case being Miscellaneous Case No.74 of 1997 in the Court of the learned District Judge, Mymensingh to bring the said Execution Case before the learned District Judge. The learned District Judge upon hearing both the parties by the order dated 08.04.1999 allowed the Miscellaneous Case No.74 of 1997 and brought back the Execution Case to his file which was renumbered as Execution Case No. 1 of 1999. While the Execution Case was pending in the Court of learned District Judge, decree holder-petitioner on 03.04.2008 filed an application in the said Execution Case under Order 21, Rule 17 read with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for amendment of the Execution Petition with a calculation sheet for passing an order of interest till realizations of the money.</u>

<u>8. The respondent filed an application for time on 07.05.2008 to enable them to file written objection against the said amendment petition. But the learned District Judge without giving the respondent any opportunity for hearing allowed the petition for amendment by the order dated 07.05.2008. The relevant provisions of Order 21, Rule 17 reads as under:-</u>

9. R.17. Procedure on receiving application for execution of decree. (1) On receiving an application for the execution of a decree as provided by rule 11, sub-rule (2), the Court shall ascertain whether such of the requirements of rules 11 to 14 as may be applicable to the case have been complied with; and if they have not been complied with the Court shall allow the defect to be remedied then and there or within a time to be fixed by it. If the defect is not remedied within the time fixed the Court may reject the application.

(2) Where an application is amended under the provisions of sub-rule (I), it shall be deemed to have been an application in accordance with law and presented on the date when it was first presented.

(3) Every amendment made under this rule shall be signed or initialed by the Judge.

(4) When the application is admitted, the Court shall enter in the proper register a note of the application and the date on which it was made and shall, subject to the provisions hereinafter contained, order execution of the decree according to the nature of the application:

Provided that, in the case of decree for the payment of money, the value of the property attached shall, as nearly as may be correspond with the amount due under the decree."

10. Order 21, Rule 11(2) provides for written application for execution of decree which shall be in writing signed and verified by the applicant or by some other persons proved to the satisfaction of the Court to be acquainted with the facts of the case and shall contains he a tabular form, some relevant particulars, including the number of the suit, names of the parties, the date of the decree, the amount of the interest (if any) due upon the decree or other relief granted thereby, together with particular of any cross decree, the amount of cost (if any) awarded etc.

11. It appears that the executing court by the order dated 07.05.2008 allowed the amendment of execution petition to the effect that the judgment-debtor-defendant-respondent is to pay interest from the date of the order till realization. In this context it is pertinent to reproduce the operating part of the exparte order dated 03.04.1983 which reads as under-

"Claim Proved

Ordered.

12. That the Misc. Case be allowed exparte with cost. The property at schedule-'B' is and be hereby attached. The O.P. shall pay up the entire dues within 60 days from the date failing which the property at schedule 'B' shall be put on sale for realisation of the dues payable by the O.P.

Sd/- A. Jaman,

District Judge, Mymensingh."

<u>13. On perusal of the aforesaid order it appears that the learned District Judge did not pass any order directing the judgment-debtor-defendant-respondent to pay interest from the date of the order till realization. In this context it is pertinent to reproduce section 34 of Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 below:</u>

<u>"34.(1) Where and in so far as a decree is for the payment of money, the Court may, in the decree, order interest at such rate as the Court deems reasonable to be paid on the principal suns adjudged, from the date of the suit to the date of the decree, in addition to any interest adjudged on such principal sum for any period prior to the institution of the suit with further interest at such rate as the Court deems reasonable on the aggregate sum so adjudged, from the date of the decree to the date of payment or to such earlier date as the Court thinks fit.</u>

<u>(2) Where such a decree is silent with respect to the payment of further interest on such aggregate sum as aforesaid from the date of the decree to the date of payment or other earlier date the Court shall be deemed to have refused such interest and a separate suit therefore shall not lie."</u>

14. While interpreting section 34 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 this Division in Sonali Bank vs. Mahbubul Amin and anr, 42 DLR (AD) 107 stated as under:

"11. It will be seen that sub-section (1) above speaks of separate interest for three different stages which may be awarded by a Court where and in so far as a decree is for the payment of money. The Court may order interest to be paid on the principal sum adjudged (1) from the date of suit to the date of the decree, in addition to (2) any interest adjudged on such principal sum from any period to the institution of the suit with (3) further interest on the aggregate sum so adjudged from the date of the decree to the date of payment or to such earlier date as the Court thinks fit.

12. Sub-section (2) clearly refers to the interest mentioned in item (3) above i.e. interest from the date of the decree and says that if a decree is silent with respect to such interest the Court shall be deemed to have refused the same and a separate suit therefore shall not lie."

<u>15. In Kadam Rosul Silicate Works and others vs. Sonali Bank, 42 DLR (AD) 294 it was reiterated in para 10 as under:</u>

<u>"The terms of the decree being silent as to further interest or any interest, it must be held under section 34(2) CPC that the court has refused such interest."</u>

<u>16. Interest under section 34 of CPC is not a statutory right payment of which can be claimed by the decree holder automatically as held by this Division in Janata Bank vs. M/s. Wahid Enterprise (Pvt) Ltd., 1995 BLD (AD) 51 in the following terms:</u>

<u>"As to interest under section 34 of the Code of Civil Procedure or as to cost of the suit and appeal plaintiff does not have any statutory right to be paid automatically. The discretion lies wills the Court."</u>

<u>17. Above decisions of this Division clearly show that the High Court Division rightly found that the order dated 07.05.2008 allowing the prayer for amendment of the application for execution suffers from error of law which has resulted in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. Accordingly, the Rule was made absolute.</u>

18. In view of the aforesaid findings and observations we are of the view that there is no illegality in the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division calling for any interference by this Court. In the premises, we do not find any merit in the leave petition.

19. Accordingly, the leave petition is dismissed.

End.
