Vs.
Md. Mizanur Rahman Talukder and others
full_judgment:
A.N.M. Bashir Ullah, J: Supplementary affidavits and counter affidavit filed on behalf of the petitioner and the opposite parties do form part of the record.

2. This Rule, on an application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure (in short, the Code) at the instance of the defendant-petitioner was issued calling upon the opposite party nos.1-11 to show cause as to why the judgment and order dated 30.11.2011 passed by the learned District Judge, Jhalokathi in Civil Miscellaneous Appeal no. 19 of 2011 affirming the judgment and order dated 03.11.2011 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Jhalokathi in Title Suit no. 96 of 2011 should not be net aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

3. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule, in short, is that the present opposite party nos. 1-11 as plaintiffs instituted a Title Suit being no. 144 of 2011 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Jhalokathi. Subsequently, the said suit was transferred in the Court of Joint District Judge, Jhalokathi and it was renumbered as Title Suit no. 96 of 2011 seeking a declaration that the power of attorney in respect of 'Ka' schedule land of the plaint is illegal and fraudulent.

4. The suit was followed by a prayer for temporary injunction under Order 39 of Rules 1 and 2 of the Code. In the prayer for temporary injunction it was averred among others that the land appertaining to R.S khatian no. 136 corresponding to S.A khatian no. 457 originally belonged to Motahar Ali Talukder and the said land was recorded correctly in his name both in R.S and S.A records of right. Motahar Ali Talukder while was in peaceful possession of the suit land orally gifted the land to his son Mojibur Rahman Talukder alias Nowab Mia, the predecessors of the plaintiffs. Mojibur Rahman Talukder died leaving the plaintiff nos. 1-11. The plaintiffs have been living at Barisal Sadar which is far away from the suit land. As such, they have been possessing the suit land through bargader. There is also a signboard in the suit land in the name and style of "Nowab Mia Vila". In the present survey the land is going to be recorded in the name of plaintiffs in D.P khatian no. 146.

5. The plaintiffs had instituted a title Suit being on 126 of 2004 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Jhalokathi Sadar which is still pending for disposal. On 03.06.2008 the defendant nos. 1-5 of the present suit corresponding to the defendants nos. 12(Kha), 15, 16, 25 and 26 of that suit filed a solenama to compromise the said suit and the defendant no. 25 of that suit gave statements in support of the said solenama on 25.3.2009. But even then the greedy defendant nos. 2-5 of the present suit fraudulently and collusively executed a general power of attorney on 26.07.2011 in favour of the defendant no. 01 in respect of the suit land.

6. The defendants have never possessed the suit land. The defendant no. 1 on the strength of the said power of attorney have been taking preparation for transferring the suit land to others and made an active attempt on 07.10.2011. So, the defendant no. 1 is required to be restrained by an order of injunction so that he cannot create any deed in respect of the suit land and cannot create any obstruction with the peaceful possession of the defendants in to the suit land.

7. The trial Court on being receipt of the prayer for temporary injunction on 09.10.2011 asked the defendant no. 1 to show cause as to why the prayer for temporary injunction shall not be granted within 10 days from the date of service of the notice thereof. Thereafter, on 12.10.2011 on a prayer under section 151 of the Code the trial Court issued an order of status-quo restraining both the parties from transferring the suit land. The defendant no.1 appearing in the suit filed written objection against the prayer for temporary injunction.

8. The case of the defendant no. 1 as it appears from the written objection is that Motahar Ali Talukder was the owner and possessor of the suit land (.86 acres) and the R.S and S.A records of right have been prepared correctly in his name. Motahar Ali Talukder in his life time did not gift the suit land or transfer to anybody else. He died leaving behind 4 sons namely Gulfukkar Talukder, Lal Fukkar Talukder, Noor Mohammad Talukder and Mojibur Rahman Talukder and 3 daughters namely Hurunnesa Begum, Ratannesa Begum and Kursia Begum. Thus, each son inherited 11/2nd  share 3 equivalent to .15 ¾ acres of land and each daughter 11/1st share equivalent to .07875 acres of land left by their father.

9. The defendants are the heirs and successive heirs of Gulfukkar Talukder, Lalfukkar Talukder, Noormohammad Talukder, Furunnesa Begum, Ratannessa Begum and Kursia Begum. The plaintiffs in order to grab the suit land have introduced the story of oral gift in favour of their predecessor Mojibur Rahman Talukder. The plaintiffs have erected a house on .02 acres of land into the suit land. The defendant nos. 13,22,23,32 and 33 of the former suit being no. 126 of 2004 between the same parties had executed a general power of attorney on 26.07.2011 in favour of the defendant no. 1 of (the present suit to conduct the said suit and also for maintenance of the suit land. The power of attorney is not fraudulent and the plaintiffs have no right to challenge the said power of attorney as such the prayer for temporary injunction is liable to be rejected.

10. The trial Court upon the hearing on the said prayer for temporary injunction allowed the same restraining the defendant no.1 from transferring the suit land to anybody else and disturbing with the peaceful possession of the plaintiffs in to the suit land by its order dated 03.11.2011. The defendant no.1 as against the said order of temporary injunction preferred Miscellaneous Appeal no. 19 of 2011 in the Court of District Judge, Jhalokathi and ultimately the appeal was heard by the learned District Judge who by his impugned judgment and order dated 30.11.2011 dismissed the appeal affirming those of the judgment and order of temporary injunction passed by the trial Court. The defendant no.1 being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said judgment of the appellate Court below moved this Court and obtained the present Rule.

11. The Rule is resisted by the opposite party nos. 1-11.

12. Mr. Md. Shahidul Islam, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner supports the Rule. He submits that both the trial Court and the appellate Court below erroneously found the prima-facie case in favour of the plaintiffs, but they did not at all consider that Motahar Ali Talukder being owner and possessor of .86 acres of land did not make any gift in favour of Mojibur Rahman Talukder, the predecessor of the plaintiffs. He categorically submits that neither in the plaint nor in the prayer for temporary injunction, there is the date of the said gift and there is nothing in the pleadings to show that at where, when and at whose presence the suit land was gifted to his only son Mujibor Rahman leaving his 3 other sons and 3 daughters.

13. He further submit that in fact, Motahar Ali Talukder did never gift the suit land to his only son Mojibur Rahman Talukder and the plaintiffs have not been possessing the entire suit land on the strength of the said oral gift. Since the plaintiffs are also co-sharer like the other defendants they are in possession of their portion as one of the co-sharer of the suit land.

14. He further submits that the plaintiffs filed another title suit being no. 126 of 2004, subsequently the said suit was renumbered as 92 of 2011 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Jhalokathi for declaration of their title and the said suit is still pending for disposal. The plaintiff have filed the present suit praying for declaration that the power of attorney is fraudulent and collusive but since the former suit is for declaration of the plaintiffs title into the suit land, the former suit was the proper suit for seeking protection of the suit land. But the plaintiffs being baffled in order to obtain an injunction in the former suit have chosen die present suit for obtaining an injunction. The trial Court and the appellate Court below totally failed to consider that the plaintiffs have no any prima facie and arguable case in their favour as the alleged gift was never taken place and acted upon in favour of the plaintiffs or their predecessor. So, both the Courts Wow have committed error of law resulted in to the error in the decision occasioning failure of justice to the defendant-petitioners. So, the judgment and the order of the appellate Court below may kindly be set aside making the Rule absolute.

15. On the other hand, Mr. Shamim Khaled Ahmed; the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of opposite party nos. 1-11 opposing the Rule submits that admittedly Motahar Ali Talukder was the owner and possessor of the suit land who gifted the suit land to his youngest son Mojibur Rahman Talukder and pursuant to the said gift the heirs of Mojibur Rahman Talukder, that is, the present plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land with the knowledge of others including the defendants. They have been possessing the suit land through the borgader and they have also a but on the suit land while the defendants have no right, title and possession into the suit land. But they have been disturbing with the peaceful possession of the plaintiffs into the suit land.

16. He further submits that some of the defendants executed a general power of attorney in favour of the defendant no. 1 in order to transfer the suit land to others. Thus, the plaintiffs have been constrained to file the present suit seeking relief against the said power of attorney followed by a prayer for temporary injunction and both the Courts below being convinced as to the prima facie of arguable case of the plaintiffs prayer for temporary injunction granted the same in favour of the plaintiffs. So, the order of the appellate Court below does not call for interference from this Court. So, the Rule is liable to be discharged.

17. I have considered the above submissions and arguments of the learned Advocates of both the parties with profound attention and have gone through the materials on record.

18. Ongoing to the materials on record it is found that it is admitted by both the parties that Motahar Ali Talukder was the owner and possessor of .86 acres of land which is the suit land of the former suit as well as of the present suit between the parties. It is also admitted that Motahar Ali Talukder died leaving 4 sons and 3 daughters and Mojibur Rahman Talukder, the predecessor of the plaintiffs was his youngest (fourth son) while the defendants of the present suit are the heirs and successive heirs of the remaining 3 sons and 3 daughters of Motahar Ali Talukder.

19. The bone contention of the submissions of the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-opposite parties is that Motahar Ali Talukder gifted the entire suit land to his youngest son Mojibur Rahman Talukder and the plaintiffs as his heirs have been possessing the suit land. But some of the defendants have created a power of attorney in favour of the defendant no. 1 in order to disturb with the peaceful enjoyment of the suit land by the plaintiffs. So, the possession of the plaintiffs into the suit and should be protected granting temporary injunction under Order 39 of Rule 1 and 2 of the Code.

20. In the case of Uttara Bank-Vs-Macneill & Kilbun, 33 DLR(AD) 298, the Appellate Division laid down a guide line for granting temporary injunction which is as follows :

"Injunctions are granted when the Court is satisfied (1) that the applicant has a prima facie case to go into trial; (2) that the protection is necessary from irreparable injury before his legal rights can be established; (3) the mischief or inconvenience likely to arise from withholding injunction will be greater than which is likely to arise from granting it."

21. In my consideration, the principle laid down for grating injunction in the above reported case is uniformly followed by this Division and in a prayer for injunction emphasis has also been given on the question as to whether the applicant has a prima facie and arguable case. But the expression "prima facie" has not been defined in the Code or any other law. The word 'prima facie' is a Latin word, but the dictionary meaning of the same is 'on the first view' or 'at first sight or 'what seems at first sight to be true' or 'apparently' etc. Thus, it can safely be said that when the plaintiff or applicant as the case may be can show that he has a prima facie case, only then he can deserve an order of temporary injunction to protect his right and interest into the suit land till final hearing of the suit and it is also fact that there cannot be any hard and fast rule as to which fact constitutes prima facie case in favour of the applicant, rather it depends upon the facts and circumstances of that particular case.

22. Now, coming to the particular case of the present suit it appears that Motahar Ali Talukder was the owner of the suit land. He had 4 sons and 3 daughters. The very simple and plain case of the plaintiffs is that Motahar Ali Talukder orally gifted the land to his youngest (fourth son) son Mojibur Rahman Talukder. From the pleadings of the plaintiffs there appears no date of such gift or no event as to when and how and in whose presence such a gift was made in favour of Iris one son leaving the other sons and daughters.

23. In this connection, the teamed Advocate for the plaintiff-opposite parties tried to argue that it is the matter of evidence which will be visualized at the time of trial. It is fact that the evidence of a fact cannot be articulated in the pleadings but whenever it is asserted that someone has gifted his entire land to his own son leaving the other co-sharers such gift is not a matter of evidence only but it is a material fact which requires to be articulated in the pleadings to make it trustworthy and believable. It is the command of law also as has been laid down in Order 6 Rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure that every pleading shall contain a statement in a concise form of the material facts on which the party relies for his claim. So, under the garb of tortuous and vapory logic, the non-mentioning of the particulars of the alleged gift which is the material facts of the suit also in the pleadings has undoubtedly weakened the plaintiffs case.

<u>24. In my consideration had there been any such oral gift in favour of only son Mojibur Rahman Talukder leaving the other sons and daughters, the plaintiffs could have stated the date of gift and the event when the same was taken place. But since the plaintiffs could not state the date of gift I find it difficult to place any reliance on such type of gift. So, in this particular case the prima facie case of the plaintiffs means a believable fact as to the oral gift of the suit land in favour of the predecessor of the plaintiffs. But the plaintiffs could not show any tangible fact and evidence that Motahar Ali Talukder had made any oral gift in favour of his only son Mojibur Rahman Talukder. So, I find that there appears no prima facie and arguable case infavour of the plaintiffs for granting temporary injunction to protect their right into the suit land.</u>

<u>25. For the other legal reason the date of the oral gift is now important. It is pertinent to point out that the from 1st July, 2005 the registration of oral gift under section 17 of the Registration Act is compulsory. If the alleged oral gift is being taken place after the said date it has become invalid for its non registration. Every fact must have a date but there is no data of the oral gift of the plaintiffs. So the story of gift is nothing but a concocted story only which have been introduced very cunningly to deprive the other heirs of Motahar Ali Talukder.</u>

26. Since, the plaintiffs as the successive heirs of Mojibur Rahman Talukder have a share into the suit land and possibly they may get 11/2nd shares into the suit land from Motahar Ali Talukder. So, on that count, the plaintiffs are the rightful owner and possessor at about .15¾ acres of land into the suit land. But the plaintiffs have been claiming the right, title and possession into the entire .86 acres of land instead of their .153/4 acres of land. It is also fact that a co-sharer can get protection of his lands against other co-sharer when there is a well identification and demarcation of his land. Since the plaintiffs did not seek any protection for his .153/4 acres of land rather he has been claiming the protection for the entire .86 acres of land so, it appears to me that there is no prima facie and arguable case in favour of the plaintiffs for granting injunction for the entire suit land.

27. From the materials on record it appears that both the trial Court and the appellate Court below failed to consider that there appears no minimum prove of the oral gift by Motahar Ali Talukder in favour of his one son Mojibur Rahman Talukder and thereby they committed an error of law resulted into the error in the decision occasioning failure of justice to the defendant-petitioners. In the present suit the subject matter of the suit is the power of attorney but injunction was sought for so that on the strength of the power of attorney the defendant no. 1 cannot transfer the suit land to anybody else and he cannot make any disturbance with the peaceful possession of the plaintiffs into the suit land and though the present suit is not a suit for declaration of the plaintiff's title into the suit land but ultimately the plaintiffs sought relief protecting their right and interest in respect of the suit land. However, be that as it may, from the materials on record I am convinced that the plaintiffs have no prima facie and arguable case in their favour for getting injunction in favour of them to protect their interest for the entire suit land. So, I find merit in the Rule.

28. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The impugned judgment and order appellate Court below dated 30.11.2011 and concomitantly the judgment of the trial Court below in respect of granting injunction is hereby set aside and the prayer for temporary injunction filed by the plaintiffs is also rejected.

29. The order of status-quo passed by this Court on 15.12.2011 is hereby vacated.

30. Let a copy of this judgment and order be sent to the Court concerned with the lower Courts record for information and necessary action.

End.

full_judgment:
Muhammad Abdur Rouf J:- This appeal by leave has been preferred by 3 (three) substituted heirs of the plaintiff late Dr. Md. Ismail Khan from the judgment and order of a learned Single Judge of the High Court Division dated 12-8-91 passed in Civil Revision No. 482 of 1988 discharging the Rule and upholding thereby the judgment and order dated 24-4-88 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar Mymensingh, allowing the Misc. Case No. 127 of 1984 under Rule 13, Order IX of the Code of Civil Procedure and setting aside the ex-parte decree passed on 17-8-72 in O.C. Suit No. 29 of 1972.

2. The predecessor of the present Respondent Nos. 1(a) to 1(j) late Abul Yunus Talukder and his full sister the Respondent No. 2 as the plaintiff Nos. 2 and 1 respectively brought the S.C.C. Suit No. 16 of 1968 against Dr. Md. Ismail Khan (since dead), predecessor of the present appellants and his son the appellant No. 2 A.B.M. Emdadul Huq as defendant Nos. 1 and 2 respectively for their ejectment from the suit premises as the monthly ejectable tenant on the ground of default in the payment of monthly rent. The suit was decreed ex-parte on 15-7-69. Thereafter those defendants as plaintiffs instituted the O.C. Suit No. 29 of 1972 against said Yunus Talukder and the Respondent No. 2 as defendants for declaration that the said decree of the S.C.C. suit was illegal, void etc. and permanent injunction for restraining the defendant decree-holders from executing said decree which was also decreed ex-parte on 17-8-72. Against which on 9-8-73 the Misc. Case No. 217 of 1973 under Rule 13, Order IX of the Code of Civil Procedure with an application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act was filed by the defendants stating, inter alia, that on 4-6-72 police arrested the defendant Yunus Talukder under Collaborator Order, 1972 and till 11-7-73 he had been in jail custody and as such he was prevented from appearing on 17-8-72, when the suit was decreed ex-parte. The appellants contested the case. It was once allowed ex-parte on 2-11-77. But upon an application filed there against on 31-1-79 by the appellants under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure the ex-parte order was set aside on 8-8-79 and thereby the Misc. Case was restored to its number and file. Subsequently it was renumbered as Misc. Case No. 127 of 1984 and ultimately it was allowed on contest on 24-4-88. Against which the appellants moved the High Court Division and obtained a Rule in the aforesaid Civil Revision case, which was discharged on contest by the judgment and order appealed from.

<u>3. Leave was granted virtually to consider as to whether in view of the decision of this Division that interest in a monthly tenancy is heritable and the fact that the ex-parte decree obtained in O.C. Suit No. 29 of 1972 has no direct bearing on landlord-tenancy relationship, the High Court Division erred in law in not holding that the Misc. Case initiated under Rule 13, Order IX C.P.C. had abated for not making all the heirs of deceased plaintiff Dr. Md. Ismail Khan as parties to the case.</u>

4. Citing the decision of this Division in the case of Prodip Das and others vs. Kazal Das Sharma and others reported in 44 D.L.R. (AD) 1, Mr. S.R. Pal, learned Advocate of the Appellants, sought to argue that the decree passed in O.C. Suit No. 29 of 1972 being an indivisible one and all the heirs of the decree-holder late Dr. Md. Ismail Khan having not been made parties in the Misc. Case No. 127 of 1984 the same stood abated and as such both the learned Assistant Judge and the High Court Division committed an error of law in not dismissing the said Misc. case.

<u>5. On the other hand Mr. T.H. Khan, learned Advocate appearing for the Respondents, referred to the statements made in para 7 of their Counter-Affidavit filed before the High Court Division, (from the additional paper book) the applications filed by the respondents in the trial Court for substitution of the heirs of said Dr. Ismail Khan and the orders passed by that court allowing substitution of those heirs. On the basis of those records Mr. Khan submitted that five sons and the wife of said Dr. Ismail Khan were duly made parties in the Misc. case on 21-3-74 vide Court's Order No. 29 dated 21-3-74 and one son and three daughters were made parties vide Court's order dated 11-6-80. The copies of the relevant applications were duly served upon the present appellants. They did not challenge those orders and as such they are not legally entitled to raise objection now upon absolutely baseless and wrong assumption, that those heirs of deceased Dr. Ismail Khan having not been made parties in the Misc. case it stood abated.</u>

6. On the face of Order No. 29 dated 29-3-74 and Order No. 80 dated 11-6-80 of the trial Court and the corresponding applications, annexure-X and X-2 respectively in the additional paper book filed on behalf of the Respondent, Mr. S.R. Pal found it difficult to press the point further that for non-inclusion of the heirs of late Dr. Md. Ismail Khan the Misc. Case stood abated and thereby the trial Court illegally allowed the Misc. case which has been upheld by the High Court Division by the impugned judgment and order. Identical objections were also taken before the trial Court on behalf of the present appellants and the same was turned down holding that on 21-3-74 five sons and the wife of said Dr. Ismail Khan had been made parties in the Misc. case and thereafter upon an objection raised by the Respondent No.3 another son and three daughters of said late Dr. Md. Ismail Khan had been added as parties in the Misc. case on 11-6-80. Moreover said Md. Yunus Talukder in para 7 of his Counter-Affidavit filed before the High Court Division clearly stated that left out heirs of said Dr. Ismail Khan had been added as parties in the Misc. cases by the Order of the trial Court dated 11-6-80 and the appellants who were petitioners before the High Court Division did not controvert such statements of said Yunus Talukder. It appears that those facts were lost sight of in the High Court Division, and the question of substitution of all the heirs of deceased Dr. Ismail was unnecessarily taken up for consideration.

<u>7. It needs to be mentioned that the Misc. case in question was once allowed ex-parte on 2-11-77, and after more than one year upon an application moved by the appellants on 31-1-79 under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure the ex-parte order was set aside on 8-8-79 and the case was restored to its number and file. Thereafter the appellants took objection that another son and three daughters of late Dr. Md. Ismail Khan were not made parties in the Misc. case. To meet such objection an application was filed on 8-6-80 for adding those left out heirs as parties and the copy of application was served on the Advocate of the appellant on 9-6-80 and the same was allowed by the trial Court by Order No. 80 dated 11-6-80. The appellant did not take any step against that order of the trial Court and rather they accepted it.</u>

8. Thus, in the facts and circumstances of the case we find little substance in this appeal. Accordingly, it is dismissed with costs.

End.

full_judgment:
Soumendra Sarker, J: The Rule issued calling upon the Opposite Party No.1-3 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 23.09.2001 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Khulna in Title Appeal No.214 of 1989 reversing the judgment and decree dated 27.06.1989 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Batia Ghata, Khulna in Title Suit No.60 of 1986 should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper.

2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present petitioners being plaintiffs filed the original suit for declaration that the kabla deed No.4761 and 4768 dated 11.07.1970 are illegal, fraudulent, collusive and ineffective contending inter-alia that the land of suit holding originally belonged to one Biraj Mistry in 8(eight) anas share and Indu Mistry to the extent of 8 (eight) anas share each. That before C.S. operation Indu Mistry died leaving only son Panchanon and accordingly the C.S. khotian was prepared in the name of Biraj Mistry and Panchanon. Subsequently; Biraj Mistry for want of money with a condition for getting the land back executed and registered two kabla deeds dated 11.07.1970 A.D. in respect of 4.91 acres of land at a consideration of Tk.6,000/-(six thousand) in favour of the principal defendants. The land of homestead and pond with its bank was in khas possession of Biraj Mistry and possession was delivered in respect of "bilan" land. The further case of the plaintiffs is such that the 2(two) deeds were written by the deed-writer but the contents of the deeds were not read over to the executant of the deeds. There was an oral agreement that Biraj Mistry or his heirs will borga cultivate the "bilan" land under the principal defendants and the homestead land will be under the control and possession of the executant. Accordingly; Biraj Mistry used to reside in the homestead land and cultivate the bilan land. During liberation war in the year 1971 Biraj Mistry left this country and died in a refujee camp. After liberation of Bangladesh some of the heirs of Biraj Mistry did not return back to this country and the plaintiffs after coming back from India started to reside in the homestead of their grandfather Biraj Mistry and while they wants to cultivate land the defendant took some signatures of them in blank demi papers in order to create a borga contract. The plaintiff No.5 & 6 in good faith signed the papers. Subsequently; on 23rd Paush, 1389 B.S. the defendant No.1-3 disclosed that they will not allow the plaintiff to borga cultivate the "bilan" land and also disclosed to evict the plaintiffs from the homestead. Thereafter; the plaintiffs obtained the certified copies of the disputed kablas & came to learn that the defendants in the kabla deeds fraudulently inserted the homestead land and pond along with its bank. In fact the executant Biraj Mistry never sold out the homestead land, pond and its bank in favour of the defendants. The defendants to grab the valuable property have created the false kabla deeds.

3. Vis-a-vis; the contrary case of the defendants in short is thus that Biraj Mistry in order to reside in India decided to sell out his properties including the homestead land and accordingly 4.91 acres of land including the homestead, pond and its bank was transferred by him by 2(two) registered kabla deeds dated 04.07.1970 which was registered on 11.07.1970 at a consideration of Tk. 6,000/- (six thousand) in favour of the defendants. The original owner of the property Biraj Mistry after delivery of possession left this country for India with his family members forever. In the schedule of the said kabla deeds some of the 'danga' plots were written wrongly as bilan land. The defendants constructed their homestead over the suit land and use to reside therein. After the liberation of Bangladesh some of the heirs of Biraj Mistry returned back to this country and requested the defendants to give permission to reside temporarily in some portion of the suit land. The defendants at the request of the plaintiffs and local elites permitted the plaintiffs to reside in some portion of the suit properties, which is situated to the South-East corner of the half portion of land appertaining to C.S. plot No.203. Accordingly; the plaintiffs executed an "Acknowledge-nama" deed but subsequently the plaintiffs out of all motive instituted the original suit on false allegation.

4. The learned Assistant Judge, Batiaghata, Khulna after taking evidence during trial of the original suit decreed the suit on contest by his judgment and decree dated 2796.1989 and 04.07.1989 respectively.

5. Being aggrieved the defendants preferred an appeal being Other Class Appeal No.214 of 1989 in the Court of learned District Judge, Khulna which was  transmitted to the 1st Court of learned Additional District Judge, Khulna and the learned appellate court by the impugned judgment and decree dated 23.09.2001 & 30.09.2001 respectively allowed the appeal reversing the judgment and decree passed by the trial court and dismissed the suit.

6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and decree the plaintiff-respondent-petitioners have preferred this revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the Rule with an interim order of status-quo.

7. Mr. Abul Kalam Mainuddin, the leaned Advocate appeared on behalf of the petitioners while Mr. Probir Neogi, the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the opposite party No. 1-3.

8. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the learned lower appellate court during dismissal of the appeal committed illegality in deciding the merit of the appeal in favour of the defendant-appellant inasmuch as the learned Additional District Judge failed to appreciate the case of the plaintiffs and the evidence on record resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate further submits that the court of appeal below in reversing the judgment and decree of the trial court was not justified. The trial court in his judgment and decree after proper sifting of evidence and appreciation of law decided the merit of the suit rightly in favour of the plaintiffs and accordingly decreed the suit. The learned Advocate also submits that the lower appellate court without rebutting the findings of the trial court reversed the judgment and decree illegally hi getting the disputed kabla deeds registered the defendants practiced fraud upon the executant of the deeds and the executant Biraj Mistry had no intention to dispose of the homestead land along with pond and its bank. The learned Advocate further submits that the defendant No. 1 in his testimony admits that the sons of Surja Kanta i.e. the plaintiff No.6 & 7 used to reside in the homestead of Biraj Mistry. The story of giving permissive possession as alleged from the side of the defendants though not proved the learned appellate court without proper analysis of evidence on records relying upon the pleadings of the defendants decided the merit of the appeal arbitrarily. The learned counsel for the petitioners lastly submits that the cited decisions of the lower appellate court do not attract the instant suit due to different facts and circumstance of the case. The plaintiffs who are the present petitioners by adducing sufficient evidence succeeded, but ignoring that the appellate court below illegally dismissed the suit and that in passing the impugned judgment and decree there has been mis-reading and non-reading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice and as such the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside.

9. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned counsel for the petitioners the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite-parties opposing the Rule controverted the argument advanced from the side of the petitioners and submits that the original suit as it was instituted is barred by the provisions laid down in order XXIII, Rule 1(3) of the Code of Civil Procedure. The plaintiffs earlier filed another suit which was withdrawn by them admittedly and the provisions cited above clearly states that only for formal defect the party can withdraw their suit & for sue afresh there must have a permission of the court before which the earlier suit filed, which is absent in the instant case. The learned Advocate further submits that in view of the statement made in paragraph No.5 of the plaint the plaintiffs are precluded to institute a fresh suit on the same cause of action and secondly; the relief sought for by the plaintiffs is not adequate to award decree in their favour inasmuch as the kabla deeds are admittedly the registered documents for more than 30 years. The prayer portion of the plaintiffs as mentioned within their pleadings is also barred under section 91 and 92 of the Evidence Act as no oral agreement can be entertained in the instant nature of the suit and by adducing oral evidence the relief claimed by the plaintiffs cannot be considered under the established decision of our Apex court. In this regard the learned Advocate referred the decision given by our appellate division in the case of Nasir Ahmed vs. Mst. Ismat Jehan Begum reported in 21 DLR (SC) 145. Moreover; under section 60 of the Registration Act and section 114(e) of the Evidence Act there is a presumptive value of correctness of the kabla deeds which has been challenged from the side of the plaintiffs. The learned Advocate also submits that the plaintiffs in order to have a decree shall have to prove their case under the purview of sections 101, 102 and 103 of the Evidence Act by adducing credible tangible evidence but the evidence adduced from their side is not at all adequate to hold such a view that the plaintiffs have been able to discharge their onus in proving their case. The learned appellate court which is the final court of facts after proper assessment of evidence and appreciation of law rightly decided the merit of the appeal on the preponderance of evidence both oral & documentary and thereby committed no illegality or irregularity in reversing the judgment and decree passed by the trial court. The learned Advocate lastly referring some decisions of our Apex court reported in 39 DLR (AD) 78 and 223, 1983 BLD (AD) 105 and the decision reported in 10 DLR (Privy Council) 01 argued that the pleadings of the plaintiffs as to the contents of the deeds are required to be proved conclusively and the allegation on fraud must be clear and proved by evidence. The trial court on glaring misconception of law in shifting onus of proof committed gross illegality which has been rectified by the impugned judgment and decree passed by the appellate court inasmuch as the witnesses produced from the side of the plaintiffs are totally incompetent to prove by the plaintiff's case and from the face of the testimonies of witnesses it is apparent that the plaintiffs have hopelessly failed to prove their pleadings. The lower appellate court under the purview of law adverting evidence on records rebutted the findings of the trial court and reversed the judgment and decree and in passing the impugned judgment and dismissal decree there is no misreading or non-reading of evidence or non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice by which it can be held that the impugned judgment and decree deserve interference of this court under the ambit of Section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure.

10. Heard the learned Advocates of both sides, perused the case records, exhibited documents, deposition of the witnesses and all other connected papers.

11. On perusal of the case records it transpires that the original suit for declaration was instituted by the plaintiffs for getting a declaration that the kabla deeds being No.4761 & 4768 dated 11.07.1970 are illegal, collusive and ineffective on the plea that the original owner of the property one Biraj Mistry never sold out the property in favour of the defendants described in the schedule of the deeds rather it was an intention of the executant of those deeds that on a condition to re-convey the land subsequently the deeds would be registered and the land measuring 4.91 acres though included within the schedule of the deeds the executant have no intention to transfer the homestead land including pond and its bank and only the "bilan" (vacant cultivable) land was transferred temporarily at a consideration of Tk.6,000/-(six thousand). The pleadings of the plaintiff-petitioners is such that the defendants collusively practicing fraud upon the executant in collusion with the deed-writer managed to obtain the deeds in question in their favour and the contents of the deeds were not read over to the executant.

12. The teamed trial court in his observation and findings relying the contention of the plaintiffs decreed the suit in their favour but it is obvious to note that the witnesses adduced from the side of the plaintiffs were not discussed or evaluated before arrival at his decision in support of the plaintiff's case, but the legal proposition is such that under order XX, Rule 05 of the Code of Civil Procedure the court is on bounden duty to assess the evidence on record in deciding the fate of each and every issue and thereafter the court of law should arrive at its own & independent decision with proper reasoning’s but obviously the trial court in this regard committed illegality by-passing the evidence adduced from the sides of the parties. It is the established principle of civil law that the plaintiff is to stand on his own leg and he cannot bank upon his adversary. In this context; if we evaluate the evidence adduced from the side of the plaintiff-petitioners we find that the witness No.1 Romesh Chandra Biswas is the plaintiff No.2 of the suit who deposed on behalf of all the plaintiffs. This witness at a stage of his deposition states that, at the time of registration of the deeds he was a minor boy of 8-9 years. The witness No.2 Thakur Das Mondal frankly conceded in his deposition that he can't state about the quantum of the suit land and he does not know anything about the talk of sale as he was not present at that time. He also cannot say anything about the alleged permissive possession of the plaintiffs. The witness No.3 Narayan Halder in his deposition similarly states that he was not present at the time of transfer and he also cannot say anything about the talk of sale between the parties. The last witness of the plaintiffs is witness No.4 Taroni Biswas and this witness also have hopelessly failed to state anything about the disputed kabla deeds and the schedule properties which is incorporated therein. Vis-a-vis; the defendant-opposite-parties to substantiate their claim have adduced 4 (four) witnesses those who were thoroughly cross-examined from the side of the plaintiffs but none of them appears to have been discredited rather their evidence appears to be sound & cogent.

13. Having gone through the statement of these witnesses I have the reason to incline such a view that the defendant's witnesses are competent & trustworthy in comparison to the P.Ws. None of them are discredited in respect of the positive assertion relating to the defendants pleadings. The lower appellate court in his observation and discussions assessed the evidence on records properly in its true perspective and rightly appreciated the actual position of law. It further appears that on preponderance of evidence the decision was taken by the learned lower appellate court which is apparently based on correct proposition of law.

<u>14. Scrutinizing the papers it transpires that within the content of the pleadings of plaintiffs in paragraph No.5 of the plaint there exist a clear mention to the effect that prior to this; they filed another suit being Civil Suit No.282 of 1984 on the same cause of action which was withdrawn by them followed by an order of the court having no permission in writing to sue afresh. In this context it is evident from the provisions laid down in order XXIII, Rule 1 Sub Rule (3) that, 'where the plaintiff withdraws from a suit, or abandons part of a claim, without the permission referred to in sub-rule (2), he shall be liable for such costs as the Court may award and shall be precluded from instituting any fresh suit in respect of such subject-matter or such part of the claim.</u>

<u>15. Having gone through the decisions of our Apex court in several case laws reported in 39 DLR (AD) 78 and 223, 1983 BLD (AD) 105, 21 DLR (SC) 145 and A.I.R. 1937 Privy Council 146 as referred by the learned counsel Mr. Probir Neogi on behalf of the opposite-parties as well as the decision cited from the side of the learned counsel on behalf of the petitioners Mr. Abul Kalam Mainuddin reported in 50 DLR (High Court Division) 134 I'm constrained to draw such interference upon the respective pleas of the parties to the suit that the contention as alleged within the pleadings of the plaintiffs for having the relief as prayed for is not at all proved by credible cogent evidence and under the ambit of order 41, Rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure the appellate court below rightly assessed the evidence on records in its true perspective and arrived at a conclusive findings and decision as to the subject matter of the suit & on the points of adjudication. There is no confusion in holding that the trial court in deciding the fate of the suit committed gross illegality. For want of adequate evidence and the legal embargo which is apparent in getting the decree as prayed for has been totally overlooked by the learned trial court. Subsequent to that; the lower appellate court while disposing the appeal discussing the evidence on record legally held that the deeds in question cannot be declared illegal for want of adequate proof. There is no such tangible trustworthy evidence upon which the case of the plaintiffs can stand, rather; obviously their evidence is topple.</u>

16. In our revisional jurisdiction under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure scope for interference is limited. Only where it is noticed that the findings and decisions arrived at by the lower appellate court suffers from gross mis-reading or non-reading of evidence or non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice or those have been founded on misconception or misinterpretation of any material evidence or contrary to law, in that case only the judgment and decree of the lower appellate court can be interfered with but apparently from the 4(four) corners the impugned judgment and decree no such aforesaid illegalities or infirmities is noticed by which it can be held that the impugned judgment and decree deserve interference of this court. The submissions advanced from the side of the learned Counsel Mr. Probir Neogi appears to be consistent which have got every nexus in the relevant laws as well as materials on records and the argument having much substance deserve appreciation of this court.

17. Having regard to the facts, circumstances and discussions referred to above the Rule have got no merit to succeed.

18. In the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and decree dated 23.09.2001 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Khulna in Title Appeal No. 214 of 1989 reversing the judgment and decree dated 27.06.1989 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Batia Ghata, Khulna in Title Suit No.60 of 1986 is hereby affirmed.

19. The order of status-quo granted earlier at the time of issuance of the Rule stands vacated.

20. Let a copy of the judgment along with the Lower Court's Record be sent down at once.

End.

full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Wahhab Miah, J: This appeal by leave has arisen out of the judgment and order dated 17.10.2011 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 666 of 1991 making the Rule absolute.

2. Facts relevant for disposal of this appeal are that respondent No. 1 as the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 667 of 1978 in the Court of Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), 2nd Court, Dhaka for specific performance of contract impleading deceased Qamrun Nessa as defendant No. 1 and the other respondents as defendant Nos. 2-4. The suit was decreed ex-parte on 23.04.1979. Defendant No. 1 (hereinafter referred to as the defendant) filed an application under Order-IX. rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure (the Code) for setting aside the said ex-parte decree on the averment, inter alia, that summons of the suit was not served upon her and her appearance in the suit as well as the filing of written statement therein was shown by forging her signatures. The application was registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 22 of 1985.

3. The miscellaneous case was contested by the plaintiff-respondent by filing a written objection, denying the allegation of non-service of summons upon the defendant and also filing of the vokalatnama and the written statement hi the suit by forging her signatures. The specific case of the plaintiff was that summons of the suit was duly served upon the defendant and accordingly, she appeared in the suit and filed written statement. Qamrun Nessa who filed the application for setting the ex-parte decree was not defendant No. 1 who entered into an agreement with her and that she was an imposter.

4. The learned Subordinate Judge by his order dated 24.11.1999 allowed the miscellaneous case and set aside the ex-parte decree and restored the suit to its original file and number. Against the order of the learned Subordinate Judge allowing the miscellaneous case, the plaintiff-respondent filed Civil Revision No. 666 of 1991 before the High Court division. A learned Judge of the Single Bench of the High court Division by the impugned judgment and order made the Rule absolute and set aside those of the learned Subordinate Judge.

5. Having been aggrieved by the impugned judgment and order, deceased Qamrun Nessa filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 222 of 2002 before this Court and leave was granted on 18.08.2004 giving rise to this appeal to consider the submissions of the learned Advocate-on-Record appearing for her to the effect:

"He submitted that the High Court Division erred in holding that summons of the original suit had been served upon the defendant No. 1 and reversed the finding of the trial court without adverting to the reasoning’s given by the trial court in this regard. He further submitted that the High Court Division should have discharged the Rule on the ground of fraud and forgery.

6. He further argued that the High Court Division should have found that the defendant's signature on the written statement was forged"

7. In the meantime, Qamrun Nessa died leaving behind her heir Mohammad Ayub Siddique and he has been substituted in her place.

8. Mr. Abdur Nur, learned Advocate-on-Record, appearing for the appellant, has placed the materials on record, namely, the application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code, the written objection filed thereto, the depositions of the PWs and the OPWs, the order of the learned Subordinate Judge and the impugned judgment and order of the learned Judge of the Single Bench and has made same submissions on which leave was granted.

9. From the order of the learned Subordinate Judge, it appears that he allowed the miscellaneous case on the finding, inter. cilia, that the defendant-petitioner was the actual lessee of the suit property and the vokalatnama in the suit was filed collusively through one Yousuf Ali Advocate; Almas and Enamul Haque were mentioned in the summons as the persons in whose presence the same was served upon the defendant by hanging at the house of PW3 being house No. 1012 Nazrul Islam Road, as she allegedly refused to accept the summons, but Alms

and Enamul Haque were not examined, so it was proved that she (Quarun Nessa) did not refuse to accept the summons in presence of the said two witnesses; from the evidence of PW2, it was found that process server-Md. Jamal Hossein who served the summons upon the defendant by hanging was in service at Munshiganj Judgeship, the plaintiff-opposite party could easily examine him, but he was not examined and his signature was proved by another process server, namely, OPW2- Ramesh Chandra Datta; though the plaintiff-opposite party challenged the identity of the petitioner Qamrun Nessa, she did not produce the original Qamrun Nessa as claimed by her and she(the plaintiff) also failed to prove by examining any other witness that Qamrun Nessa who appeared on 23.02.1979 in the suit was the actual Qamrun Nessa. So it was proved that no summons was served upon the petitioner; the signature of the defendant appearing on the lease deed and her specimen signatures was examined by a hand writing expert and the report went against her; after long 17 years, it was quite natural that there would be scone change in everything, but there was great similarity between the signatures appearing on the lease deed, the signatures given in the deposition sheet in the instant case and the specimen signatures, whereas there was no similarity with the signatures of Qamrun Nessa given in the vokalatnama on 23.02.1979; the case was filed on 29.04.1980, i.e. within 30(thirty) days after the defendant had come to know about the ex-pane decree on 01.04.1980 as evident from the information slip dated 01.04.1980; the defendant-petitioner proved that she could know about the ex-parte decree after making search in Court through her Advocate; the summons was shown to have been served by practising fraud and fraud vitiates everything.

10. The learned Judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division made the Rule absolute on the finding, inter alia, that from the record, it appeared that the service return of the summons in the suit was filed and proved in the miscellaneous case by the plaintiff through OPW2-Ramesh Chandra Datta., a process server of the Court as exhibit-'chha'. The learned Judge believed the endorsement made on exhibit-'chha' that one Md. Jamal Hossain, a process server of the Court, went to the address of the defendant for serving summons and since she was not available at the address, he tried to serve the same on her uncle, Ali Newaz after explaining the contents of the summons. Since uncle, Ali Newaz declined to receive the summons, the process server-Md. Jamal Hossain served the same by affixing on the main gate of the house in which the defendant was residing in presence of the two attesting witnesses, namely, Almas and Enamul Haque of the some address; in the application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code and also in the deposition of PW she did not specifically deny the case of the plaintiff that process server, Md. Jamal Hossain "came to her house and sought to serve the summons upon her uncle, Ali Newaz as defendant No. 1 was not at home and having failed to do so" served the same affixing it on the main entrance of the house in which the defendant was residing and that there were none, by the names: Almas or Enamul Haque at that address who allegedly attested the service of summons by hanging; the defendant in her application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code did not specifically deny the case of the plaintiff that she appeared and filed written statement in the suit, but merely stated in her application as well as in her deposition that she never received any summons of the suit; the defendant in her application as well as in her evidence did not make out any case when she first came to know the fact of the ex-parte decree and in absence of any evidence with regard to the date of her knowledge about the ex-parte decree, it could not be found whether the miscellaneous ease was filed within time or not; the finding of the learned Subordinate Judge that the defendant was able to prove that no-summons of the suit was served upon her was erratic and perverse; PW3 sought to deny in his evidence that there was no service of summons by hanging, but he was not competent to say so; more so, when such case was not made out by the defendant in her application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code; the application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code showed that 01.04.1980 was written subsequently by hand with different ink as the date of her knowledge, but she did not lead any evidence to that effect; therefore, the date of her knowledge regarding ex-parte decree was not proved; the defendant did not mention either in her application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code or in her evidence about any information slip of the Court saying that she for the first time came to know about the ex-parte decree on 01.04.1980 as per the information slip and the information slip was not also exhibited in the miscellaneous case, the date of knowledge in respect of the ex-parte decree, was not proved, either by oral or documentary evidence by the defendant; the finding of the learned Subordinate Judge that the defendant proved the date of her knowledge about the ex-parte decree and that the miscellaneous case was filed within time, was without any evidence and perverse and as such, not tenable in law.

11. By now it is well settled that in case of allegation of non-service of summons by the defendant, the onus is always upon the plaintiff to prove that summons was duly served upon him. In the instant case, the plaintiff in sub-pars ii, iii and v of pars 10 of her written objection stated as under:

"ii. That the summons on all defendants were duly legally and validly served.

iii. That thereafter petitioner defendant no. 1 appeared by Vokalatnama and also filed written statement though (sic, it would be through) appointed lawyer appointed by her.

v. That all summons on the defendants were duly served but none of them did come forward to contest the claim of the plaintiff'

12. From the above, it is prima-facie clear that the plaintiff did not say in the written objection as to how the summons of the suit was served upon the defendant; in the written objection, it was simply stated in general term that the summons was served upon all the defendants.

13. The plaintiff-opposite party did not examine her as a witness in the case and none-else was also examine& on her behalf and thus she did not own the fact on oath that summons of the suit was served upon the defendant. On behalf of the plaintiff-opposite party (in the miscellaneous case) service return of the process server was proved and marked as exhibit-Thha' and the signatures of the process server-Md. Jamal Hossain was proved and marked as exhibit-' Chha (1)'. Interestingly, the process server-Md. Jamal Hossain was not examined. One Ramesh Chandra Datta, a process server of Dhaka Judgeship was examined as OPW2 and he proved those as exhibits. OPW2 stated in his deposition that he law the hand writing of Md. Jamal Hossain and his signatures and accordingly, he proved those as exhibits. In the service return, process server-Md. Jamal Hossain stated that he had gone, to the address of the defendant to serve the summons upon her and she being not available at the address, he (the process server) tried to serve the same on her uncle-Ali Nawaz after explaining the contents of the summons, since Ali Nawaz declined to receive the summons, the same was served by hanging on the door of the main entrance of the house in which the defendant was residing in presence of two attesting witnesses: Almas and Enamul. The learned Subordinate Judge found that from the evidence of OPW2, it appeared that Md. Jamal Hossain was still employed at Munshiganj Judgeship and the opposite party could easily examine him, but he was not examined.

14. We have gone through the evidence of OPW2. This OPW in clear terms stated in his examination-in-chief that Md. Jamal Hossain who was process server of the Judgeship (Dhaka Judgeship) was promoted to the post of clerk and then he was posted at Munshiganj, but he could not say where he was serving at Munshiganj. So, we find that the learned Subordinate Judge was correct in making the above observation. Since Md. Jamal Hossain was till in service, it was not at all difficult to find him out and also place of his posting and then examine him in the case. The learned Subordinate Judge further noticed that as per, report of the process server, Almas and Enamul Haque were the two attesting witnesses in whose presence summons was served by hanging, but the plaintiff-opposite party did not examine them. In view of the report of the process server-Md. Jamal Hossain as stated hereinbefore, it was incumbent upon the plaintiff-opposite party to examine him and also to examine the attesting witnesses to prove the service of notice by hanging. In view of the report given/endorsement made in the service return by the process server-Md. Jamal Hossain, OPW2-Ramesh Chandra Datta could be accepted as a competent witness to prove the fact of service of summons of the suit by hanging upon the defendant within the meaning of rule 19 of Order V of the Code. The learned Judge of the Single Bench did not at all consider the provisions of rule 19 of Order V which has mandated that where a summons is returned under rule 17 (in the case the summons was returned under rule 17), the Court shall, if the return under that rule has not been verified by the affidavit of the serving officer, and may, if it has been so verified, examine the serving officer on oath, or cause him to be so examined by other Court, touching his proceedings, and may make such further inquiry in the matter as it thinks fit; and shall either declare that the summons has been duly served or order such service as it thinks fit. The learned Judge of the Single Bench accepted the evidence of OPW2 as if the report given in the service return or the endorsement made thereon was a formal one like the postmortem report which can be proved tinder section 509A of the Code of Criminal Procedure without examining the Civil Surgeon or the other medical officer who made such report in the circumstances stated therein. The learned Judge made a fundamental error in accepting OPW2 as a competent witness in place of the process server Md. Jamal Hossain, to prove the service of summons upon the defendant by hanging and that error misled him to come to the finding that the summons was served upon the defendant by hanging.

15. The learned Subordinate Judge also considered the testimony of PW3, the owner of House No. K/12 of Nazrul Islam Road (defendant No.1 used to reside there at the relevant time) who stated that no summons was served in that house and that no summons was hanged and that none named Almas or Enamul was his tenant(s). These are all questions of fact and the learned Subordinate Judge considering all these facts came to the definite finding that summons of the suit was not served upon the defendant. The learned Judge of the Single Bench in exercising revisional jurisdiction under section 115(1) of the Code was not justified to interfere with the said finding of fact.

16. It is very pertinent to state that in the written objection, no assertion was made to .the effect as reported in the service return by the process server-Md. Jamal Hossain. The only assertion made in the written objection was that summons of the suit was served upon all the defendants, but unfortunately, the learned Judge proceeded in the case accepting the report of the process server as the positive case of the plaintiff-opposite party (in the miscellaneous case) and found fault with the defendant that she neither in her application nor in her evidence specifically denied the case of the plaintiff that "the process server Md. Jamal Hossain came to her house and sought to serve the summons first on her uncle Ali Nawaz as the defendant No.1 was not at home and having failed to do so served the same by affixing the same on the door of the main entrance of the house in which the defendant No. 1 was residing and that there were none by the name Almas or Enamul Huq at that address who allegedly attested the service of summons by hanging" This is absolutely shocking that the learned Judge of the Single Bench accepted the report of the process server as the pleading of the plaintiff-opposite party without caring to see what her pleading in the written objection was. This was a serious legal flaw in the approach of the learned Judge in sifting the evidence on record in deciding the point whether summons of the suit was served upon the defendant and led him to come to the erroneous finding that "the learned Subordinate Judge, nonetheless found that the defendant No.1 was able to prove that no summons of the suit was served on her. Such Finding is therefore erratic and perverse."

17. For the reasons stated hereinbefore, we find substance in the first submission on which leave was granted.

18. In the written objection, it was stated that the defendant appeared by vokalatnama and filed written statement through the lawyer appointed by her. The learned Judge of the Single Bench observed that "Defendant no. 1 in her application in the Misc. case also did not spec deny the case of the plaintiff that defendant no. 1 appeared and filed written statement in the suit. "This observation is totally erroneous inasmuch as at the time of filing the application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code, the defendant could not have and did not have the idea what would be the case of the plaintiff- opposite party in the written objection. In making the above observation, the learned Judge of the Single Bench did not care to see the statements made in Para-3 of the application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code. In the Para, it was specifically stated to the effect "That the O. P. No. 1 also submitted a Vokalatnama and a written statement on behalf of the petitioner as the defendant no.1 in that title suit which was not duly signed by the petitioner that signature was also forged one."

19. When the plaintiff-opposite party in her written objection specifically stated that the defendant appeared in the suit through her lawyer and filed written statement, the onus was squarely upon him to prove the said fact. More so, when the defendant in her application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code categorically stated that she did not sign the vokalatnama and the written, statement filed in the suit and her signatures thereon were forged. But the plaintiff examined neither herself nor anyone else in the case to own her said case stated in the written objection. On the other hand, the defendant examined herself in the case as PW1 and in her examination-in-chief categorically asserted that it was not correct that she engaged a lawyer named Yousuf Ali and she gave her a vokalatnama, but the learned Judge did not at all consider her evidence to the above effect.

20. It further appears that the learned Subordinate Judge observed that immediately after the refusal to accept the summons, the defendant was shown present in Court on 23.02.1979 by filing application for time through her lawyer Yousuf Ali, Advocate, but her signatures appearing in the original lease deed were not similar with those of the signatures given in the vokalatnama, had the person who signed the vokalatnama on the said date was the actual Qamrun Nessa than them could be similarity in between the signatures of the vokalatnama and the original lease deed. This was quite permissible in view of the provisions of section 73 of the Evidence Act. The learned Subordinate Judge further found that from the evidence of PWs 2 and 3, it was proved that the defendant-petitioner of the application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code was the real Qamrun Nessa and although the plaintiff challenged that the defendant was not the actual Qamrun Nessa, she failed to produce the original Qamrun Nessa. The above findings and observations of the learned Subordinate Judge are based on proper consideration of the evidence on record and on correct appreciation of section 101 of the Evidence Act.

21. For the discussions made above, we find substance in the third submission on which leave was granted.

<u>22. So far as the limitation in filing the application under Order IX, role 13 of the Code, is concerned, it appears that in paragraph I of the application, it was categorically stated that "The petitioner on searching came to know on 01.4.1980 that the Title Suit No. 667 of 1978 was filed by the O. P. No. 1 defendant of the suit and she arranged to get decree and order ex-parte without not notifying the petitioner in due course on 23.04.1979. "Defendant-petitioner as PW1 categorically stated that she did not get summons of the suit and no summons was served upon her on 19.09.1979, she knew nothing about the ex-parte decree and she came to know about the ex-parte decree after searching in Court. The learned Subordinate Judge being the last Court of fact considering the information slip filed in Court which was obtained on 01.04.1980 found that the case was filed within 30 (thirty) days from the date of knowledge; but unfortunately, the learned Judge of the Single Bench without considering the case of the defendant-petitioner as made out in her application under Order No. DC, rule 13 of the Code observed that "The defendant no. 1 also did not make out any case in her application in the Misc. case nor led .any evidence as to when she came to brow about the ex-parte decree." It may be stated that in the revision application, no, objection and ground was taken as to the finding of the learned Subordinate Judge that the application was filed on 29.04,1980 within 30 (thirty) days from the date of knowledge of the ex-parte decree from the information slip obtained on 01,04.1980, so the suit was not barred by law.</u>

<u>23. The teamed Single Judge on total misreading of the case of the defendant-petitioner gave an adverse finding that the date of knowledge was a subsequent interpolation in her application for restoration of the suit, though no such case was made out in the revision application. The finding of the learned Judge that "Even if it is assumed that the application filed in the Miscellaneous case mentioned the date of knowledge of the defendant no. 1 in respect of the ex-parte decree but since this was not proved either by oral or documentary evidence by the defendant No. 1 is the result of non-consideration of the case of the plaintiff as made out in her application udder Order 1X, ride 13 of the Code and the deposition of PW1 in that respect.</u>

24. Considering the evidence on record, the learned Subordinate Judge came to the clear finding that (i) a vokalatnama was filed through collusion thus presence of the defendant was shown in the suit, (ii) the service of summons of the suit upon the defendant was shown by resorting to fraudulent means. The findings of fraud as given by the learned Subordinate Judge appear to us based on proper consideration of the materials on record. The learned Judge did not reverse the said findings of fraud of the learned Subordinate Judge. Fraud vitiates everything. Therefore, we find substance in the second submission on which leave was granted.

25. For the discussions made hereinbefore, we find merit in the appeal and accordingly, the same is allowed. The impugned judgment and order is set aside and those of the learned Subordinate Judge are sorted.

End.
