full_judgment:
Soumendra Sarker, J: The Rule issued calling upon the Opposite Party Nos.1-14 to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 03.06.1998 and 20.09.1998 respectively passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Court, Barisal in Title Appeal No.42 of 1996 affirming the judgment and decree dated 31.01.1996 and 06.02.1996 respectively passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Barisal in Title Suit No.91 of 1994 should not be set aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this court may seem fit and proper.

2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present petitioner as plaintiff instituted the original Title Suit No.91 of 1994 in the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Barisal against the present opposite-party Nos. 1-3/11-20 and one Chand Baru bibi, the predecessor opposite party Nos. 4-10 for declaration of title in the land described in schedule "ka" of the plaint and for declaration that the auction sale mentioned in schedule "Kha" of the plaint is collusive, fraudulent and false with a further declaration that the V.P. proceedings described in schedule "Ga" of the plaint is illegal, without jurisdiction and not binding upon the plaintiff contending inter-alia that the suit property originally belonged to one Jogendra Nath who purchased the same in the benami of one Mathura Nath and Sukumar out of his own money. The R.S. record was prepared in the name of Mathura Nath. Subsiquently, Jogendra Nath executed a will in favour of one Shachindra Nath in the year 1356 B.S. and thereafter Jogendra Nath died on 14.04.1960 A.D. Shachindra Nath filed a Probate case being No.32 of 1960 in which Probate was granted on 11.01.1962. Subsequently while Mathura Nath and Sukumar challenged the execution of will and also denied to execute a deed of nadabi in favour of Shachindra Nath a Title Suit being No. 97/98 of 1963 was filed by Shachindra Nath. That suit was decreed in favour of Shachindra. Thereafter Shachindra mutated his name in S.A. khatian No. 210. Shachindra Nath transferred the suit property in favour of the defendant Nos.9-11 who sold out the same in favour of the plaintiff on 25.02.1964. Subsequently the plaintiff mutated his name and paid rent to the Government. The plaintiff came to know that the suit land was auction sold in favour of the defendant Nos.1-5 on 29.05.1955 in a Rent Suit No. 91 of 1954 and by virtue of a Execution Case No. 339 of 1955 auction purchasers mutated their names in the S.A. khatian for the suit land. The Rent Suit was false, collusive and created. The further case of the plaintiff is such that the original owner of the land was all along a citizen of this country and he never migrated to India and as such the suit land cannot be a vested property. The plaintiff in the 1st part of Chaitra, 1396 B.S. came to learn about the vested property proceeding as well as the auction purchase of the defendant Nos.1-5 and thereafter he filed the original suit against the defendants.

3. The contrary case of the contesting defendant No.6 in short is such that one Kalma Jamindari Company Ltd was the superior landlord of the suit property. After the acquisition of Jamindari estate by the Government the superior landlord exhausted his interest and right, title over the disputed property and taking compensation money he surrendered the property in favour of the Government and the Government since then possessing the land as khash land under the Government. That .49 acres of land has been declared vested property rightly and the Government granted lease for that portion of land and the lessee is possessing the same. The plaintiff having no manner of right, title, interest and possession in the disputed properly on the basis of some forged created papers filed the suit on false allegation which is liable to be dismissed.

4. The learned trial court after taking evidence dismissed the suit on contest by its judgment and decree dated 31.01.1996 in Title Suit No. 91 of 1994.

5. Being aggrieved the plaintiff preferred an appeal being T.A.No. 42 of 1996 in the court of learned District Judge, Barisal. The appeal was transmitted to the court of learned Additional District Judge, Barisal and the learned Additional District Judge vide, the impugned judgment and decree dated 03.06.1998 disallowed the appeal affirming the judgment and dismissal decree of the trial court.

6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and decree the plaintiff-appellant-petitioner has preferred this revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the Rule with an interim order of stay.

7. Mr. A. Y. Ahmed Ali, the leaned Advocate appeared on behalf of the petitioner while Mr. Khandaker Aminul Haque, the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the opposite party No.1.

8. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the learned courts below during disposal of the original suit and its subsequent appeal committed illegality in not considering the plaint case and the evidence adduced from the side of the plaintiff-petitioner. The learned Advocate during his argument pressed paragraph No. 8 of the revisional application wherein it is stated that the plaintiff-petitioner in his plaint and evidence stated that Shachindra Nath, the predecessor of the plaintiff filed Title Suit No.97 of 1962 for declaration of title and confirmation of possession against Mathura Das and others. That suit was decreed ex-parte on 22.12.1962 but the certified copy of the aforesaid decree was not filed in the trial court. On 01.10.1996 the plaintiff-appellant-petitioner accordingly filed the application along with a certified copy of the aforesaid decree under order 41 rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure and at the time of hearing of the appeal the appellant prayed for marking the certified copy of the decree as exhibit but the learned lower appellate court did not consider the application and marked the paper as exhibit which is an error on the face of the record and that has resulted serious miscarriage of justice. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the plaintiff-appellant-petitioner to prove his case prays for an order of remand so that he can able to prove his case and falsified the case of the defendants.

9. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party opposing the Rule controverted the submissions advanced from the side of the petitioner and submits that the trial court as well as appellate court during disposal of the original suit and its subsequent appeal committed no illegality or irregularity. There is no misreading or non-reading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in deciding the merit of the appeal against the appellant and in favour of the respondent and there is nothing to interfere with the impugned judgment and decree passed by the lower appellate court which is the final court of facts. The learned Advocate further submits that the plaintiff-appellant-petitioner filed the application under order 41 Rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure on 01.10.1996 A.D. before the appellate court and the appellate court hearing the parties to the case passed his judgment on 20.09.1998. By this time from 01.10.1996 to 20.09.1998 the plaintiff-appellant remained dormant and took no step for hearing and disposal of that application. The teamed Advocate also submits that the contents of the application is not consistent with the plaint of the plaintiff and in the plaint along with the appeal-memo the plaintiff-appellant did not state the actual number and year of the Civil Suit allegedly instituted by Shachindra Nath. Even the date of its decree was not cited therein. The content of the application under order 41 Rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure is vague upon which no concrete decision can be taken and as such the learned lower appellate court did not pass any order for the aforesaid ambiguity. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the plaintiff's plaint does not disclose any definite cause of action as in paragraph No. 11 of the plaint there is no insertion of month of alleged cause of action of the plaintiff for which the plaintiff allegedly constrained to institute the original suit.

10. Heard the learned Advocates of both sides, perused the case record, deposition of the witnesses, exhibited documents and all other connected papers.

<u>11. On perusal of the case record it transpires that both the trial court as well as the appellate court in their observation and findings concurrently held that the plaintiff to the suit utterly failed to discharge his onus in proving his case and also failed to prove the auction purchase by the defendant Nos.1-5 as void, fraudulent and collusive. It is the case of the plaintiff that the auction purchase by the auction purchasers in Rent Suit No.91 of 1954 is collusive and the defendant Nos. 1-5 who are claiming the property by way of auction acquired no land, but scanning the evidence on records it is observed by both the courts below that the plaintiff-appellant-petitioner failed to prove his bonafide by adducing credible evidence that the defendant Nos.1-5 collusively auction purchased the land in dispute. Furthermore; as to the pleadings of the plaintiff it is evident from the face of the record that there is no tangible evidence to substantiate as to when Jogendra Nath purchased the suit property in the benruni of Mathura Nath and Sukumar. The plaintiff has failed to submit the alleged kabla deed. Moreover; the plaintiff-petitioner asserted that Shachindra Nath obtained Probate in respect of the suit property but on perusal of the plaint and the schedule of it, the paper showing the alleged Probate marked as exhibit-2(ka) go to show that the land included in the schedule of that are different with that of the schedule of the plaint. It has been well defined within the findings of the appellate court which is consistent with the papers on record.</u>

12. Having gone through the original plaint of the plaintiff-petitioner 1 find that in his pleadings there is a recital of the plaintiff that while Mathura Nath and Sukumar Das denied to execute “না-দাবী মুক্তি পত্র” in favour of Shachindra Nath, Shachindra Nath filed a Title Suit in the 3rd court of the then Suboidinate Judge, Barisal being Title Suit No.97/98 of 1963 and obtained decree therein. It is to be noticed here that the aforesaid decree is the basis of plaintiff’s case. In consultation with the application under order 41 Rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure there is a glaring discrepancy which is the number of Title Suit as cited by the plaintiff-petitioner in the said application and that Title Suit is 97 of 1962. Apart from this; I have come-across from the pleadings of the plaintiff that the plaintiff failed to state the month in which his cause of auction was allegedly accrued. In this context; it is needless to advert that the contention of the plaintiff-petitioner apparently suffers from material contradiction and omission which cannot be ignored. The submissions advanced from the side of the learned Advocate for the opposite-party have got every nexus with the case records. The learned courts below in deciding the fate of the suit and its subsequent appeal rightly held that the plaintiff to the suit since not able to prove his case he is not entitled to get any relief as prayed for. The assessment of evidence as it appears within the findings of the lower appellate court appears to be fair and legal and no such misreading or non-reading of evidence and non-consideration of material fact is noticed by which it can be held that the impugned judgment and decree suffers from any sort of infirmity and illegality. Before departing with the case I like to advert that to fill up the lacuna there lies no scope to allow the application under order XLI, Rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

13. Having regard to the facts, circumstance and discussions referred to above I am constrained to hold such a view the Rule having no substance is liable to be discharged.

14. In the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs. The judgment and decree dated 03.06.1998 and 20.09.1998 respectively passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Barisal in Title Appeal No.42 of 1996 affirming the judgment and decree dated 31.01.1996 and 06.02.1996 respectively passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Barisal in Title Suit No.91 of 1994 is hereby affirmed.

15. The order of stay granted earlier by this Court at the time of issuance of the Rule stands vacated.

16. Let a copy of the judgment along with the Lower Court's Record be sent down at once.

End.
